scope: All 148 historical groups and 742 frozen primary atoms retain independent dispositions and historical assessments. 145 group classifications are complete; P08, CN15 and MD01 remain partial for timing derivation, pre-authentication cap refusal and metadata numeric domains. The supplemental template inventory separately classifies all 169 template.md lines and 34 source predicates, without inheriting primary evidence or enlarging the frozen primary IDs. Cryptographic source review and finite userspace transport campaigns are recorded, not independent crypto certification or physical/network universality. Conditional withdrawal/printed-QR evidence, external references, open primary interpretations and deployment/hardware evidence keep overall conformance partial.

interpretation_sources.purpose: Normative Language plus definitions, role versions and protocol evolution. The supplemental template inventory classifies all 169 lines and 34 source clauses; its related primary IDs do not inherit fulfillment/evidence.

working_assumptions.decision: Keep application-configured immutable startup/minimum-buffer hints for this SDK profile. Do not require an automatic arrival-delay estimator before continuing targeted software work; do not add output delay to either hint.
working_assumptions.reason: The pinned C++ config reports a configured or pipeline-derived startup lead, explicitly not a measured one, and a configured min_buffer_ms (default 500). Its player state uses these values. This supports a practical static-profile assumption, not normative permission to ignore estimator recommendations or a reason to copy its 500-ms default into Go. Go values remain deployment inputs, not measured optimums.
working_assumptions.revisit: Authoritative clarification of P:65, adding runtime estimation, a changed output pipeline, or deployment underrun/startup measurements. Physical latency and convergence remain separate obligations.

working_assumptions.decision: Support nonnegative int64 progress/duration/per-thousand-speed fields, including zero duration and paused speed zero. Retain rejection of negative fields, complete required progress grammar and silent protocol-error closure; do not clamp or silently default malformed received fields.
working_assumptions.reason: C++ stores and reads all three progress fields as uint32_t, so negative playback speed is not represented in that path. Its read_uint_field instead logs/drops invalid fields and the containing progress object keeps defaults, unlike this SDK's fail-closed parser. This is evidence for a nonnegative working domain only, not equivalence of error behavior or proof of a normative range. Go intentionally keeps exact values beyond uint32 and floating-point precision boundaries; no C++ integer cap is imported.
working_assumptions.revisit: An authoritative signed-field/range clarification, a real peer requiring negative/reverse playback, or a deliberate compatibility-policy decision. Existing rejection tests cannot resolve the normative domain.

working_assumptions.decision: Keep the accepted PSK-only SDK profile. Audio output or an artwork consumer does not automatically enable a usable pairing-code display/speaker; any future code channel and format require explicit host integration.
working_assumptions.reason: C++ offers dynamic code only when configured channels and formats are both nonempty, and otherwise may offer a configured static code. Its display/speech callbacks are application-owned. This is a useful library/product boundary, not proof that the device-level SHOULD recommendations are universally inapplicable. Neither code method is implemented by these Go policy tests.
working_assumptions.revisit: A product requests code-based pairing with a defined operator interface, or specification clarification requires a different library-profile reading. Reassess usable out-channel and QR recommendations then.

working_assumptions.decision: Keep AllowUnpaired immutable per Client and locally owned. Do not add a runtime setter solely to close the applicability question; do not claim that ordinary shutdown implements live revocation.
working_assumptions.reason: C++ exposes an explicit live setter. Its disable path finds relying sessions and closes them with pairing_required; enable/restart behavior has direction/pairing exceptions. This gives a concrete model if a live feature is selected, but does not prove that every library must offer that operation. Our native tests establish advertisement and resistance to remote policy mutation only.
working_assumptions.revisit: A live policy-change API is requested or the immutable-profile reading is rejected. Before implementing it, test relying-session selection, rekey barriers and the exact required reason; shutdown is not a substitute.

working_assumptions.decision: Return the literal version-0 pairing-token string from the SDK. Physical labels, QR rendering and product presentation belong to the host integration; do not add a generic printer/renderer API.
working_assumptions.reason: C++ provides a token string API and gives dynamic QR token rendering to the application listener. That architecture supports separating secret encoding from presentation, but a dynamic version-1 callback does not settle the separate physical printed-PSK version-0 MUST. Our token tests prove encoding only, not physical QR compliance.
working_assumptions.revisit: A product prints or displays the PSK token, or a concrete QR integration is added. Verify its actual QR payload verbatim, without wrapper/URI, in that product; do not mark the physical requirement fulfilled from a string test.

working_assumptions.decision: Keep the current bounded pre-Noise capacity refusal and do not import the C++ pre-Noise text-goodbye path. No cleartext application goodbye may be added to bypass the initial encrypted-message sequence.
working_assumptions.reason: C++ releases an excess nursery connection before start_noise_handshake with ANOTHER_SERVER. Its host disconnect invokes send_goodbye_reason, and send_app_json routes to plain text while Noise is inactive. That source path conflicts with our pinned RC1 sequence, so copying it cannot resolve lower-priority refusal semantics. Current cap behavior remains an explicit provisional resource policy, not declared full compliance.
working_assumptions.revisit: Clarification of the pre-authentication capacity exception versus required encrypted refusal reasons, or an explicitly reviewed admission/resource design. Do not weaken caps or emit early cleartext merely to imitate another implementation.

requirements.statement: initial order, text handshake, encrypted binary application messages, complete WebSocket messages
requirements.notes: `internal/wire/channel.go`, `session.dispatch`; `TestEncryptedChannelAndFailureHandling`; official protocol baseline. A scripted Go peer now checks premature JSON/unknown binary/cleartext before hello, before first activation and after rekey, for both suites and WebSocket directions, with no further data response or persistence/session leak. Direct TLS is rejected before upgrade. This peer shares the Noise primitive, not SDK framing; explicit multi-frame RFC 6455 boundary injection remains untested.

requirements.statement: no early application writes; ignore extensions only after activation, including re-handshake gates
requirements.notes: `session.dispatch`, `session.request`; `TestUnknownTypesIgnoredOnlyAfterActivation`, `TestDisplacementWaitsForRehandshakeActivation`. Shutdown now closes silently during re-handshake (`TestShutdownDoesNotWriteBeforeHelloOrDuringRehandshake`). The internal request dispatcher now independently rejects pre-hello/pre-activation calls as well as rekey-gated calls; this is defense in depth beyond the public active-session/actor ordering.

requirements.statement: valid UTF-8 JSON object, string `type`, object `payload`; unknown type need not be non-empty or contain `/`
requirements.notes: `protocol.Parse`; `TestEnvelope`, `TestReferenceUnknownExtensionsAreIgnored` with same-direction barrier. Missing/null/non-string type remains an error.

requirements.statement: ignore unknown exact-case payload keys, not invalid known values
requirements.notes: `protocol.Decode`; exact-case/null/nested tests and `FuzzTypedDecode`. Explicit conditional-ignore rules defer field validation (M16); server hello exact-case lookalikes and unimplemented-role support handling are covered by M13. The question-mark notation marks omission, not permission to send null for a known typed field; conditional-ignore exceptions remain explicit in each handler.

requirements.statement: emit only defined fields; no invented future wire negotiation
requirements.notes: `sendHello`, `sendState`, role commands; `Config.Specification` rejects unsupported profiles before storage. All outbound payload variants still need a field-by-field trace audit.

requirements.statement: ignore unimplemented binary IDs; recognized IDs remain recognized when role inactive; discard still authenticates and validates
requirements.notes: Wire allowlist and role handlers; unknown/inactive audio failure E2E, `TestUnknownFragmentStillTracksSequence`, tamper/replay channel tests. Source IDs are not implemented or advertised. Final atomic review citation correction: inactive implemented IDs remain recognized; the previously stated rule needs its actual source.

requirements.statement: size limit, fragment flags, no nested/interleaved sequences, one in flight per direction, no fragmentation for small sends
requirements.notes: `protocol.Fragment` / `Reassembler`; boundary roundtrips, malformed sequence tests/fuzz, encrypted fragmented send/receive. A scripted peer independently encodes fragments for full-size Noise rekey JSON; oversized transport remains rejected. Separate real-WebSocket/net.Conn faults stop the second fragment of a three-fragment client hello for both the masked outbound and unmasked inbound SDK writers: no last fragment or logical sent observation follows, even after a fully delivered second carrier whose Write reports error. Positive controls reassemble all three. Inbound runs actual ServeHTTP after an unmodified HTTP upgrade and verifies mode release. Unknown fragments may discard data but retain sequence state.

requirements.statement: clock requests frequent enough for convergence
requirements.notes: Actor's startup exchanges and periodic minimum-uncertainty bursts; independent startup E2E. Long-running disturbance/network-asymmetry behavior still needs measurements.

requirements.statement: use time-filter and withhold player availability until ready
requirements.notes: `internal/timesync`, `timeSample`, `sendState`; pinned/live C++ oracle and independent server availability traces. SDK scheduling uses checked mappings that retain reference arithmetic in its defined range, reject nonfinite/nonpositive clock rates and refuse out-of-range integer casts/additions. The same checked paths are asserted in every live C++ query. Algorithm parity and safe arithmetic do not establish physical accuracy (P16–P19).

requirements.statement: capture arrival after decryption/reassembly, before actor/observer delay
requirements.notes: `Channel.ReadTimed`; `TestTimeSampleUsesCapturedArrivalNotActorTime`, channel timed/fragmented observations. Server transmit stamping is S.

requirements.statement: core dispatch independent of roles; stream lifecycle in delivery order even while discarding
requirements.notes: Single session actor; media/unavailability E2E and role removal tests. Role-specific bodies are implemented only for advertised roles.

requirements.statement: init version 1, exact public key encoding, inner Noise fields, message-2 literal `{}`, silent failure
requirements.notes: `wire.Handshake` / `exchange`; raw-prologue/literal-response tests, resolver binding and both-suite pairing E2E. Scripted peer matrices cover malformed initial/rekey fields, tamper and wrong suite/prologue. Positive controls verify literal message 2 under old keys, raw whitespace/unknown fields and full-size Noise carriers. Post-upgrade net.Conn faults now cover both WebSocket directions at client/init, initial/rekey message 2, hello and initial/new-key state: zero/prefix/full-carrier errors, cancellation and deadline. Inbound uses actual ServeHTTP, passes through HTTP 101 and verifies its live mode reservation, unmasked carrier and cleanup. Failed rekey writes do not commit the candidate category. This shared-Noise-library simulation is not independent crypto or comprehensive native socket-load evidence; server/error retry/reason classification remains separate.

requirements.statement: `server/hello` shape and optional language preferences
requirements.notes: `decodeServerHello` requires a string name, non-empty string list when languages is present, and an object for the known source support field. `TestServerHelloKnownFieldsAreValidatedBeforeReply` and independent malformed-hello E2E prove rejection before any application reply. Snapshot.ServerLanguages preserves order/spelling/duplicates across re-handshake and owns its slice. Unknown exact-case fields are ignored; source internals remain opaque because source is never offered. Language validation checks RFC 5646 structure/duplicate variants/singletons, not a registry date or extension semantics; see the policy below.

requirements.statement: hello once, correct role support objects, mandatory Pairing PSK offer, no inactive-role use
requirements.notes: `sendHello`, config role/codec checks, request guards; independent negotiation/pairing and official baseline. No source or application-specific role is advertised.

requirements.statement: admissible activities/roles for the matched PSK, first omitted roles empty, later omissions preserve or implicitly remove roles
requirements.notes: `activate`, `activationRefusal`; first-activation, refusal-order and credential-loss tests. `TestReferenceUnauthorizedPrecedesUnsupportedPairing` checks that enabling unpaired access must make the whole activation admissible before `pairing_required` applies. A concurrent native peer test holds the admission mutex while malformed roles, unauthorized paired pairing/playback and unpaired playback are refused with the correct silent/goodbye behavior, without displacing the holder or writing credentials. Unsupported attempts are not admitted.

requirements.statement: ignore pairing object outside pairing; offered method/format and malformed conditional fields
requirements.notes: `TestActivationIgnoresPairingFieldWithoutPairingActivity`, `FuzzActivationIgnoredPairingField`, independent inactive-field/malformed-field/PSK-format E2E. Missing/null/wrong-type fields close silently; unoffered methods/string formats abort without revealing a PSK. First/re-handshake refusal recovery and index 2 on the next native attempt are independently tested. Old unauthorized roles cannot survive refusal under new keys (`TestRejectedPairingActivationCannotRetainOldPermissions`). A deferred server handoff still closes with another_server after a refusal (`TestReferenceDisplacementSurvivesRejectedRehandshakeActivation`).

requirements.statement: role removal stops output, clears state/pending updates; unchanged versions preserve state
requirements.notes: `activate`, `clearRole`; independent metadata/color/artwork/visualizer removal/reactivation and output handoff E2E. A native encrypted player lifecycle test now gates one write, queues another, then ends the stream/removes the player and verifies cancellation/flush, no old acceptance and fresh playback after reactivation on the same device. Missing prior stream/end is a peer protocol error; session shutdown releases output. Simulated output does not measure physical stop latency.

requirements.statement: initial/new-role state, `available` plus complete included role states, never emit inactive-role objects
requirements.notes: `sendState` and role guards; official baseline, role activation E2E. State-less role reactivation may use latest availability; sending another full state is harmless.

requirements.statement: availability does not end streams; external interruptible/non-interruptible classification
requirements.notes: `SetAvailable`, `LeaveGroup`, ordered lifecycle while unavailable; independent ignored-extension/unavailability and artwork partial-transfer tests. Application decides whether external use is interruptible.

requirements.statement: omitted state object preserves state/pending update, included object replaces whole role state
requirements.notes: `serverState` / `scheduled`; independent current/future/replacement/clear tests. Mandatory promptly/current-state emission is S; an uncertain receiver clock is not proof a peer violated first-state timestamp rules.

requirements.statement: stream config negotiated from capabilities/state; in-place changes keep stream alive
requirements.notes: `startStream`, decoder selection; official preference PCM24→PCM16 / PCM→FLAC cases and independent format update E2E. Availability/state gating of server emission is S; races with local availability must be tolerated.

requirements.statement: clear selected active streams, not their lifetimes; non-empty unique target roles or omission
requirements.notes: `stopStream`; independent clear scenarios, decoder reset, visual queue clear. The native player lifecycle test proves a blocked write and following decoded chunk are discarded, the stream remains open and fresh audio resumes without stale replay. An artwork clear target is invalid. Application-specific stream roles are unsupported; physical downstream flush latency is unmeasured.

requirements.statement: end targeted active streams and stop/clear unless role defines different completion
requirements.notes: `stopStream`, `clearRole`; independent player stop, artwork end/resume and visualizer end tests. A native player end/removal case now checks cancellation/flush of blocked and queued audio and fresh playback after reactivation. Server's track-transition/seek policy is S; simulated acceptance/flush events are not physical stop measurements. Targeted target-grammar review reproduced and fixed shared clear/end model overvalidation and list-order-dependent partial end before detecting an uncancelled artwork transfer. The historical assessment is unchanged.

requirements.statement: complete group state with defined playback state
requirements.notes: Typed required fields and enum check in `dispatch`; group markers/reference scenarios. Exhaustive malformed group-state cases remain outstanding; promptly sending changes is S. The full required-field/type/enum matrix now covers both availability states, exact-case lookalikes, empty string names/IDs without invented restrictions, replacement/public snapshots, silent encrypted peer failures and no credential writes. Prompt server emission is still a server-owned duty, not certified by these receiver tests.

requirements.statement: paired unpair deletes matched record and sends required reason; unpaired session ignores
requirements.notes: `dispatch`; paired unpair/persistence E2E. Dedicated unpaired-unpair no-op fault test remains useful. A dedicated unpaired native session now receives server/unpair followed by a same-direction group marker, proving no disconnect, identity change, unrelated record deletion or Store.Save.

requirements.statement: required goodbye reasons and reconnect guidance, recommended shutdown, legal silent close
requirements.notes: `displaced`, `failGoodbye`, `shutdownGoodbye`, `Client.run`; arbitration/refusal/unpair E2E, permanent-error tests, re-handshake shutdown regression. Application-specific restart/user-request APIs are not provided; cancellation means shutdown.

requirements.statement: Use the first decrypted/reassembled uint8 as the RC1 binary discriminator; preserve assigned ranges without treating every allocated role ID as implemented
requirements.notes: The exhaustive application-dispatch inventory covers all 256 byte values except transport-only ID 1, which is consumed/validated by reassembly. Implemented IDs remain errors with inactive roles/malformed payloads; reserved, source and unimplemented application IDs are ignored only after activation. Existing wire tests separately cover authentication and encrypted reassembly. Allocation of a range does not imply implementation of every ID in it. Final atomic review citation correction: unknown binary ignore and inactive recognition are core rules, not inferred from allocation ranges.

requirements.statement: Implement integer-microsecond client/time and server/time fields, correlate the echoed request and keep client/server monotonic clock domains independent
requirements.notes: Known fields are validated before unrelated/late response correlation; wrong/missing/null fields cannot consume the active request. The native peer observes the actual outgoing request shape and integer values even with no active role. Timestamp-domain tests use different positive/negative origins, not a shared Unix epoch. This is message/arithmetic evidence, not physical synchronization accuracy or convergence under all network disturbances.

requirements.statement: On unavailable/leave, maintain previous-group history, move to or stop a solo group, emit group/stream updates and never automatically rejoin/restart on availability recovery
requirements.notes: These are Sendspin server topology/history and playback duties. The SDK emits availability/leave and consumes ensuing core updates, but does not implement or certify every multi-client server grouping algorithm. The native single-client leave probe is not a substitute for this server-side topology matrix.

requirements.statement: Place controller commands in client/command only while that role is active, with its current advertised command permissions
requirements.notes: The existing exact-argument/native-receive matrix covers the defined controller wrapper, omitted irrelevant arguments and role/capability changes. Unknown application-role sending is deliberately excluded in M34; this is not a claim to support arbitrary custom objects.

requirements.statement: Implement role-independent client/leave with an empty payload after activation; use of it for an external interruptible activity is application-controlled
requirements.notes: The native peer observes exact empty-payload output from no-role and controller-only clients. A following same-direction marker proves the connection remains usable and no credentials were persisted. The application decides when it no longer wants group playback; the SDK does not invent an automatic external-source policy. Server grouping effects are M29.

requirements.statement: Validate known server/command outer objects before action; process active player commands while keeping unsupported source-role internals opaque
requirements.notes: The known source outer field must be an object even though capture is not implemented (M:135). Malformed source alongside a valid player command is rejected before any player state/Store mutation. A well-formed unsupported object is not decoded or acted on; unknown application fields follow M04. Senders limiting these objects to active roles remain a server duty. This adds no source capability or wire negotiation.

requirements.statement: Tolerate in-flight inactive-role objects in client/state and client/command without rejecting solely for their presence
requirements.notes: Explicit server receive duty for the role-removal race. It does not authorize this client to send inactive objects deliberately or weaken its own checks for malformed/recognized incoming active-role messages. A client-only SDK cannot certify another implementation's full inactive-role tolerance matrix.

requirements.statement: Optionally include application-specific role objects in permitted command messages only when implementing/advertising those roles
requirements.notes: No application-specific roles are implemented or advertised; configuration rejects unsupported role/version identifiers before storage. Native hello observation confirms the selected supported-role subset and PSK-only method. The client sends no custom role objects and ignores unknown payload fields without interpreting their bodies. This is deliberate optional scope, not implementation of the custom-role protocol.

requirements.statement: one connection direction/discovery mode at a time; server-initiated recommended
requirements.notes: `Client.enter` reserves inbound/outbound mode across advertising, discovery, connection and reconnect. `TestMDNSClientInitiatedDiscoveryAndModeReservation`, cancellation and startup-failure tests. Standalone discovery helpers cannot police independently created advertisements owned by an embedding application.

requirements.statement: plain ws transport, no TLS
requirements.notes: `validateEndpoint`, direct TLS rejection before upgrade, and no automatic redirect following. `TestServeHTTPRejectsDirectTLSBeforeUpgrade`, `TestConnectDoesNotFollowWebSocketRedirects` (http/https/ws/wss targets) and permanent-endpoint tests. Externally terminated proxies/listener configuration remain the application's responsibility.

requirements.statement: announce client service, actual listener port, required path; optional name matches hello
requirements.notes: `serviceForListener`, `AdvertiseClient` and `serviceText`; isolated native DNS-SD TXT/SRV/address/unique-instance E2E, long-name test and listener-address unit matrix. Serve advertises by default; explicitly disabled/externally mounted advertising is application-owned.

requirements.statement: scoped advertisement/discovery lifetimes must not leak conflicting modes
requirements.notes: `TestServeClosesAcceptedListenerOnStartupFailure`, `TestServeWaitsOnlyForItsOwnHTTPHandlers`, mDNS cancellation/repeated-browser/socket-release tests. Stopping Serve waits for its own upgraded handlers, not unrelated HTTP mounts of the same Client.

requirements.statement: discover server service and connect to advertised address/path; hello overrides name hint
requirements.notes: `Browse`, endpoint validation, missing-path rejection and isolated real IPv4 discovery followed by Noise. Snapshot stores server/hello rather than the DNS hint. Interface-change/native OS behavior and receiving-interface scope for IPv6 link-local discovery remain open; link-local endpoints lacking scope are not emitted.

requirements.statement: at most one admitted connection, highest declared activity determines rank
requirements.notes: `Client.admit`, actor-owned activation processing and independent multi-server arbitration. The declared rank is now published atomically with the holder before another admission can compare against it. Cancellation is checked after acquiring the admission lock and before retiring the current holder; a canceled contender cannot displace it. Buffered-output handoff waits for the old worker before the next admission; Oto's expressly approximate downstream-tail limits are not a strict physical-output handoff guarantee.

requirements.statement: persist the most recent admitted playback server
requirements.notes: Accepted playback activations update the credential transaction. `TestReferenceMultiServerArbitration`, `TestAdmittedActivityUpdatesDoNotRunAdmissionAgain` and `TestLastPlaybackServerSurvivesClientRestart` check selection, demotion preservation and actual FileStore reload without identity changes.

requirements.statement: provisional until admissible activation; never arbitrate an inadmissible activation
requirements.notes: Shape/role checks and ordered refusal precede `admit`; the encrypted misbinding candidate cannot displace the holder. The new native concurrent test sends three inadmissible activations while the admission mutex is held: duplicate roles close silently with ErrProtocol, paired pairing/playback returns unauthorized, and unpaired playback returns pairing_required. The holder remains usable and non-retiring; no candidate changes records or last-playback state or starts pairing. This is a targeted concurrency matrix, not exhaustive cancellation/interleaving/resource-load evidence.

requirements.statement: higher/equal rank accepted, lower rank rejected
requirements.notes: `TestReferenceMultiServerArbitration` covers playback/idle takeover, equal-playback replacement, lower-priority refusal and persistent-record integrity. This does not imply exhaustive multi-peer stress.

requirements.statement: a started pairing attempt is protected against incoming playback/pairing
requirements.notes: Attempt start and decided retirement share Client.mu. `TestReferencePairingProtectionStartsBeforeFirstWriteReturns`, `TestReferencePairingAttemptCannotBeDisplacedByPlayback` and `TestDecidedDisplacementPreventsALatePairInit` exercise both start/handoff orderings. Protection ends on completion, cancellation or timeout.

requirements.statement: both idle: prefer only an incoming last-playback server over a different holder
requirements.notes: Idle branches in `admit`; independent idle-keep and idle-prefer-last-playback cases. This special rule does not turn every same-priority idle reconnect into a takeover.

requirements.statement: optionally admit parallel pairing alongside playback, otherwise abort/close incoming pairing
requirements.notes: Parallel admitted holders are deliberately not implemented. `TestReferenceIncomingPairingDoesNotInterruptPlayback` checks `pair/abort concurrent_attempt`, preserved playback ownership and no persisted rejected record. The additional arbitration rules for two admitted holders do not apply.

requirements.statement: later activity updates do not readmit/escalate through arbitration
requirements.notes: `TestAdmittedActivityUpdatesDoNotRunAdmissionAgain` holds the admission lock while the same holder enters/leaves/re-enters playback. Rank and last-playback persistence still update for future candidates.

requirements.statement: drop provisional sessions without an activation within 30 seconds
requirements.notes: A provisional session's budget starts after WebSocket upgrade and includes Noise plus initial activation, capped at 30 seconds. `TestInitialActivationBudgetIncludesHandshakeAndIsCapped`, `TestActorDoesNotRestartTheInitialActivationBudget`. These are not a socket-exhaustion/load bound for arbitrary HTTP clients.

requirements.statement: provisional cap and room for an evictable pairing record
requirements.notes: At most min(4, RecordCapacity-1) open SDK sessions, protected provisional record selection, native capacity exhaustion/recovery tests. A full five-record store now pairs a fourth session while three actual long-term Noise responses are gated before Channel publication: only the oldest unprotected record is evicted, with one Save and unchanged playback history. Rekey selection retains old-record protection until transport-key commit. Excess sockets are closed before Noise/authentication, so no encrypted lower-priority reason is available at that early cap. This is not evidence of every priority-refusal wire path under resource pressure.

requirements.statement: displaced/rejected goodbye or pairing-abort reason, then close
requirements.notes: Native arbitration and incoming-pairing refusal tests check `another_server` / `concurrent_attempt`; output ownership is released before completing a handoff. Re-handshake write gates defer a goodbye until activation, including rejected activation recovery. Pre-authentication resource closure is CN15, not an invented authenticated reason.

requirements.statement: server announcement and server name recommendation
requirements.notes: The client validates the endpoint it receives but does not implement a Sendspin server advertiser. Reference-server TXT/SRV checks are interoperability evidence, not certification of all server discovery policies.

requirements.statement: outbound multi-server selection implementation-defined; later protocol independent of connection direction
requirements.notes: DiscoverAndRun chooses the first usable endpoint and reconnects there; applications may provide selection via Browse/Run. No automatic server-selection UI is implemented. Native sessions in both directions use the same Noise/actor implementation.

requirements.statement: mandatory KKpsk2, server initiator independent of WebSocket direction, replay rejection
requirements.notes: `wire.Handshake`/`exchange`, both-direction native pairing and encrypted tamper/replay/cleartext failures. The reviewed Noise-library configuration is not independent cryptographic proof of forward secrecy or post-compromise behavior.

requirements.statement: implement at least one suite and announce the chosen one, without invented negotiation
requirements.notes: Both RC1 suites are supported, validated in Config, and exercised by native pairing/negotiation E2E. Initial client/init selects one; the peer is not asked to negotiate an unsupported mechanism.

requirements.statement: canonical 43-character identities, CSPRNG per-device private keys, long-lived persistence
requirements.notes: `NewCredentials`, FileStore reload and independent identity/pairing tests. Wire Base64URL canonicality is checked before server identity resolution; newlines are not treated as operator leniency. Static-key rotation changes identity rather than silently migrating a pairing record.

requirements.statement: PSK ID formula/category binding, public Sentinel, stored server binding
requirements.notes: `pskID`, category-aware resolver and native credential-loss/misbinding tests. Canonical decoder guards the received 32-byte identifier. A stored-ID mismatch is a failure, not an initial lookup miss.

requirements.statement: initial-only Sentinel fallback; mismatch alone never deletes/replaces trust
requirements.notes: Resolver and both-side credential-loss/repair E2E; existing records survive until explicit repair/unpair. Server-side retry, approval/UI and refusal of playback while its mismatched record still exists are server duties. Sentinel by itself authenticates no operator-known peer.

requirements.statement: raw init prologue; init-failure reasons are server-owned; other failures silent and time-bounded
requirements.notes: Raw prologue/literal response, canonical decoding, tamper/replay and aggregate-budget evidence. The malformed/read-stall matrix covers both suites/directions. The separate 152-case I/O matrix has 76 outbound post-upgrade handler cases and 76 inbound actual-ServeHTTP cases: zero/prefix/full-carrier errors, cancellation/deadline and failed fragmented hello, with controls at every target. Inbound preserves the real HTTP upgrade before arming, verifies the inbound mode is reserved at the write boundary and released after handler return; real masked/unmasked writer bits are checked on carriers. Closure/no later data, error propagation, unchanged idle-fixture credentials/history and released sessions are asserted. The injected net.Conn honors Close/deadlines; the RFC 6455 tracker is independently tested. This does not model actual kernel backpressure, native OS writes, every cancellation race or server/error retry/reason policy; the peer shares the Noise primitive.

requirements.statement: rekey inside old transport, prior handshake hash, no hello replay, next new-key activation gate
requirements.notes: Independent promotion/re-pairing, hello preservation and rejected activation recovery; reader/actor acknowledgement and write gates. Scripted matrices validate old-key message 2, prior-hash binding, activation resumption and premature application/old-key rejection in both suites/directions. Write-fault cases now cover both SDK writer roles: failed pr rekey response retains the old lt category/record binding through teardown, even when the peer receives message 2 but local Write fails. New-key state failure instead occurs after valid commit and still terminates without credential mutation. Inbound additionally checks ServeHTTP mode reservation/release and actual unmasked carriers. Finite shared-Noise-primitive simulations do not prove all native write/cancellation races or remote rollback.

requirements.statement: tolerate/discard old-key client applications before Noise message 2
requirements.notes: This is a server receive obligation. Restarting client clock requests avoids assuming an old request will be answered; the native late-finalize test can legitimately send an old-key timeout abort before receiving the peer's already-sent rekey.

requirements.statement: preserve connection/stream/time-filter state across re-handshake
requirements.notes: Filter preservation, request restart and verbatim hello-state E2E are targeted evidence. A new native pairing flow starts from a trusted unpaired Sentinel session and performs Sentinel-to-pairing-to-long-term rekeys while one audio write is blocked and another decoded chunk is queued. Both old-key chunks are accepted in order after release, with two observed encrypted handshake responses, no flush/reopen/cancellation or re-decoding and the player stream retained. The virtual output clock deliberately pauses at the gate: this proves buffer/lifecycle retention, not real elapsed-time scheduling, late-join/load behavior or physical accuracy.

requirements.statement: Declare only activities needed for the current purpose and drop an activity when its purpose ends
requirements.notes: This is the server's recommendation for cooperative admission. The SDK ranks exactly the declared admissible activity set and does not guess the peer's real purpose. Client activity-priority and subsequent-update behavior remain CN06-CN13.

requirements.statement: perceptual volume curve and short gain ramp (SHOULD)
requirements.notes: `Engine.render`; `TestPerceptualGainAndMuteUseAShortRamp` checks the power curve, 5-ms ramp, mute transitions and input ownership. Audibility remains P16/P19.

requirements.statement: volume changes do not clear mute (MUST NOT)
requirements.notes: Credential updates set only the requested field; independent `TestReferenceServer` now explicitly requires mute to survive the group-volume change.

requirements.statement: non-empty ordered formats, PCM/FLAC baseline, buffer capacity, optional additional Opus
requirements.notes: `Config.defaults`, `sendHello`, `Format.Validate`; official PCM16/24, FLAC and Opus cases. Decoder capabilities are narrower than every possible PCM/FLAC format; only listed formats are offered.

requirements.statement: PCM little-endian/interleaved whole frames; FLAC complete frames/STREAMINFO; one bare Opus packet; standard Base64 header
requirements.notes: Built-in decoders and codec tests, independent encoded/source hashes. Header presence and canonical standard Base64 are now checked before every factory, including custom ones; built-in FLAC also independently rejects ignored CR/LF in its public decoder API. A custom factory remains responsible for codec contents/whole-unit validation. Explicit multichannel/Opus-depth and exhaustive malformed FLAC/Opus evidence remain separated in the atomic review rather than inherited from this aggregate T.

requirements.statement: full state on changes, supported command values, required volume/mute, advertised preference only
requirements.notes: `sendState`, `request`, `PreferFormat`; reference remote/group volume E2E, official preference changes. All three player commands are currently always offered. The core player-state wrapper is emitted only for an active player, independent of local availability; generic client/state behavior remains M18.

requirements.statement: clamp and persist output delay, survive temporary buffered excess (MUST); avoid interruption (SHOULD)
requirements.notes: Clamp in local/remote setters, credentials/reconnect E2E, `TestOverflowRecoversWithinMemoryLimits`. A chunk waiting in Device.Next or the startup timer re-reads changed delay/gain and remaps the current clock estimate; explicit state changes wake the timer. Recovery can drop buffered audio; interruption quality and hardware behavior are unmeasured.

requirements.statement: volume/mute persistence (RECOMMENDED)
requirements.notes: Store snapshots include both values; persistence unit tests. State is freshly reported on each connection.

requirements.statement: empirically size/debounce lead/jitter parameters (SHOULD), never add output delay to them (MUST NOT)
requirements.notes: Values are explicit immutable Config inputs; `sendState` keeps them separate from output delay. Automatic jitter-tail measurement/debouncing is not implemented; choose values for the deployment and measure startup/underruns. No claim of minimal latency.

requirements.statement: accept only offered remote commands; exact command arguments
requirements.notes: `decodePlayerCommand` first validates the active role/discriminator, then ignores unoffered command argument bodies. Known commands still enforce exact typed/present arguments; unit matrix and independent malformed-command E2E prove no persistence/echo on failure, including while unavailable. Valid commands persist and echo full player state with zero/false intact, mute independent from volume, and signed-64-bit delay clamping before machine-int conversion. The SDK always offers all three player commands; no configurable per-command capability is implied.

requirements.statement: stream format was advertised; Opus bit depth ignored
requirements.notes: `Format.Matches`, `startStream`; independent negotiation, official cases and header-presence tests. Additional direct Opus bit-depth equivalence tests remain useful.

requirements.statement: keep old buffered audio and decode with each received format (MUST); advertise only output formats switchable without gap (SHOULD)
requirements.notes: Decoder changes do not reset engine; chunks own format/samples. `TestFormatChangeRetainsQueuedAudioAndDrainsOldDevice` checks queued values, formats and old-device drain. Drain errors now stop before reopening; Close is attempted once even on failure. A backend's independent context.Canceled is terminal unless the actual work context was canceled. Reset during drain skips obsolete format opening and flushes before fresh audio; pending Open cancellation still leaves the worker usable. Gaplessness across physical device reopen remains unmeasured; use a single rate/channel layout when unsure. Timeline continuity/no replay is S.

requirements.statement: clear drops old chunks; no audio without stream; unavailable clients discard valid data but stay connected
requirements.notes: `binary`, `stopStream`, `Engine.Reset`; independent no-stream fault and lifecycle E2E. The native encrypted clear/end/removal cases explicitly gate a write and queue a second decoded chunk; cancellation/flush prevents either old marker being accepted, then fresh playback resumes without reopening. Worker tests separately reject fresh audio after a failed Flush and ensure pre-canceled workers never open output. Decode/validation still runs when unavailable. Native driver downstream cancellation/flush timing remains outside the fake-device evidence.

requirements.statement: 13-byte header, server timestamp mapping, subtract output delay; send_ahead never changes schedule
requirements.notes: Real framing verdict and `ReadTimed`; scheduling only receives timestamp/format/samples, not send_ahead. Dedicated tests now cover output-delay subtraction (including saturation rather than int64 wrap), current delay/gain after waiting, and exact microsecond-to-time conversion beyond time.Duration's range. Unusable/unrepresentable mappings fail locally rather than becoming immediate output; the checked mapping is compared with the pinned C++ oracle in its defined range. These are software scheduling boundaries, not DAC latency compensation or physical output measurements.

requirements.statement: never use saturated send_ahead values as delay samples (MUST NOT)
requirements.notes: No send_ahead delay estimator exists; no such value is sampled. `Config.Encoded` exposes the field diagnostically only. Any future estimator must discard both 0 and 4294967295 and pre-convergence samples.

requirements.statement: late chunks should be dropped; late arrival must not shift playback
requirements.notes: `Engine.render` uses the timestamp target; `TestLateAudioIsDropped`, `TestExtremePastAudioCannotOverflowLateDrop`. Extreme stale targets must not overflow the prefix calculation; partial recovery is not a physical synchronization measurement.

requirements.statement: inaudible steady-state corrections (MUST NOT produce artifacts)
requirements.notes: Bounded discrete frame correction is implemented; listening/loopback measurements on each backend/OS are still required.

requirements.statement: ±0.5% sliding-average speed over 150 ms; rare one-shot recovery (MUST)
requirements.notes: An additional output-timeline budget bounds absolute inserted/deleted duration to 750 microseconds in each 150-ms window, across rate/channel/sign changes and stream resets; opposite edits do not cancel. Frame costs round up and history is bounded. Tests sweep chunk-boundary windows at 8–384 kHz and independently count interval intersections using exact common-rate integer ticks across mixed formats. Physical device speed, correction audibility, actual timing feedback and rare one-shot recovery under network/load disturbances remain unverified; this partial assessment is not promoted by the software window evidence.

requirements.statement: ±1-ms accuracy floor (MUST), ±0.5-ms target (SHOULD), backend latency compensation (SHOULD)
requirements.notes: Time-filter and `Device.Next` contract implemented; physical audio-output error and native clock feedback unverified.

requirements.statement: no startup pitch modulation/warble/artifacts (MUST NOT)
requirements.notes: One-shot scheduling and gain ramps exist; real startup/underrun/reopen measurements remain outstanding.

requirements.statement: duration, initial/live lead, grouping, exact outstanding-byte accounting and latest-delay recomputation
requirements.notes: These are server send/accounting obligations, not a client-side wire ACK or queue-length report. Built-ins reject >150-ms chunks. Engine memory bounds/recovery are defensive client behavior, **not** an implementation of the server's accounting ledger.

requirements.statement: suggested correction strategy
requirements.notes: Implementation uses this permitted family of strategies. The suggestion does not waive P16–P19 or prove physical conformance.

requirements.statement: Select a producible advertised format using the current preference/priority and rederive a live stream when preference changes
requirements.notes: Server-owned selection/re-encoding policy, including its permitted track/operator exceptions. The SDK advertises capabilities/preferences and accepts only advertised stream formats. Native and harness preference-change interoperability does not certify every server codec/resampling/heterogeneous-group policy.

requirements.statement: Treat supported_commands as settability rather than infer remote control from reported volume/mute or mandatory output delay fields
requirements.notes: The SDK currently advertises all three player commands, so its normal trace does not exercise every read-only amplifier topology. A server must not synthesize absent remote capabilities from state-field presence. This is not a missing SDK configuration setter or a reason to relax P09's command validation.

requirements.statement: implement incoming full state and outgoing command for the advertised controller role
requirements.notes: `decodeControllerState`, `request`, public `Command`; all 15 RC1 command names have a fixed unit inventory and are independently observed on the real encrypted reference receive path. This is client implementation, not an application/backend media engine.

requirements.statement: required state fields, typed command subset, volume/repeat domains, conditional non-negative seek maximum
requirements.notes: `TestControllerStateFieldAndReplacementMatrix`, `TestControllerRejectsNegativeOptionalSeekBound`, independent malformed-state E2E. A present negative maximum is invalid even without absolute seek; absence is legal unless seek is offered. Duplicate command-list entries are not rejected by inventing an unspecified uniqueness rule.

requirements.statement: send only currently active, currently offered commands
requirements.notes: `TestControllerRequestsUseLatestCapabilityState` and independent native capability change/removal/reactivation cases. Rejected local calls neither transmit nor disconnect. `TestControllerSnapshotCannotChangeCommandPermissions` checks defensive state/seek-pointer ownership.

requirements.statement: exact required/forbidden parameters; preserve zero, false and signed offsets; absolute seek inside the latest bound
requirements.notes: `TestEveryControllerCommandHasExactArguments`, native exact wire observations for every command, zero/maximum absolute seek and MinInt64/zero/MaxInt64 relative seeks. HTTP observation metadata uses decimal strings for numeric command arguments so JSON float conversion cannot hide lost precision; actual wire arguments remain JSON integers.

requirements.statement: replace included controller state, preserve it when omitted; clear state on role removal
requirements.notes: Typed state replacement does not merge an omitted old seek bound. Native reference reconfiguration drops seek when the range becomes unknown; role reactivation supplies a new full state. `TestControllerStateFieldAndReplacementMatrix` covers omitted-object preservation.

requirements.statement: ignore unsupported inbound controller commands and perform play/pause/stop/next/previous/repeat/shuffle/seek behavior
requirements.notes: These are server/application obligations. The SDK validates/forwards its own requests and receives state; the fixture's native server parses/routes them, but its optional backend callbacks are not a certified media player. In particular, playback history and best-effort relative-seek effects are not implemented by this client SDK.

requirements.statement: group volume redistribution/rounding, group mute and capability-dependent averages
requirements.notes: No client-side averaging algorithm is substituted for the server's reported state. Single-player native volume/mute interoperability and mute independence are tested; that is not proof of the multi-player server algorithm or rounding.

requirements.statement: switch cycling and previous-group priority
requirements.notes: The switch command is forwarded without extra arguments. Group membership/history/cycling are server-owned; the local fixture does not certify every topology. Existing LeaveGroup/availability APIs do not implement a competing client-side grouping policy.

requirements.statement: ignore unknown exact-case fields, not malformed known values
requirements.notes: Controller state/command model matrix plus `FuzzControlModels`. Known command values remain the RC1 subset; unknown strings in supported_commands are invalid, unlike the explicit player rule that ignores unoffered remote commands. Broader inactive-role/core-message field validation remains part of the ongoing audit.

requirements.statement: typed timestamp, optional text/year/one-indexed track, complete non-negative progress object
requirements.notes: Typed metadata/one-indexed track and independent malformed-state tests remain targeted evidence. The historical non-negative-progress wording describes current decoder policy, not a now-completed normative range decision: MD01.06 explicitly leaves negative progress/duration/speed applicability open because the pinned fields say integer without a stated nonnegative qualifier. No runtime range change is made in this review. Calendar-year/URL restrictions or fetching are not invented.

requirements.statement: included metadata replaces all fields; omitted object preserves current/pending state; omitted progress clears position
requirements.notes: Timestamp-only clear, full-state replacement unit matrix and native scheduled/current/clear E2E. `TestReferencePausedLargePositionIsExactAndProgressCanBeCleared` proves that omitting progress clears the live read model.

requirements.statement: current state plus at most one pending replacement, past/present immediate cancellation; current best clock estimate without convergence wait
requirements.notes: Single actor-owned pending pointer; existing scheduled/replaced/clear reference cases. `TestPresentationSchedulingUsesBestEstimateWithoutAvailabilityGate` proves per-role independence, omitted-object preservation and due updates after a first clock sample while still unconverged/unavailable. Shared checked deadline conversion preserves ordinary monotonic time, handles duration-range boundaries with an arbitrary-precision oracle and rejects unrepresentable future mappings instead of applying them immediately.

requirements.statement: position derives from applied state and server-clock time, with duration/zero clamp
requirements.notes: `Metadata.Position` uses allocation-free wide arithmetic; fixed regressions, 16,807 arbitrary-precision combinations and fuzzing check accepted-state calculation and documented helper representation, including fractional decreases and saturation. The oracle's nonpositive-duration helper policy does not resolve the negative wire-domain question in MD01.06. This is arithmetic evidence, not universal input-domain, clock or physical accuracy certification.

requirements.statement: never extrapolate a pending scheduled track
requirements.notes: `CurrentPosition` reads applied metadata only and requires an active synchronized metadata role; existing applied-versus-pending unit test and native large paused-position E2E. Absence/removal/disconnect returns no known position; the readiness requirement is the SDK read-model policy, not a reason to postpone state application.

requirements.statement: server reports playback changes, first current state, sensible scheduled lead
requirements.notes: Sender-clock stamping, promptly reporting changes and the 20-second SHOULD limit are server obligations. The receiver must not accuse a peer solely because an uncertain clock estimate maps its first state into the future. No backend playback-change coverage is inferred from receiver interoperability.

requirements.statement: role removal clears current/pending metadata; getters do not leak mutable state
requirements.notes: Native removal/reactivation and first-state clock-recovery E2E; defensive progress/snapshot tests. Availability changes alone do not deactivate a role or discard its metadata.

requirements.statement: typed timestamp and optional three-integer RGB channels, each 0..255
requirements.notes: `decodeColorState`; all six fields are checked for null, scalar, wrong length/type and out-of-range values in the unit matrix, with independent representative fault E2E. Valid black/white/full palette values survive the native reference transport unchanged.

requirements.statement: included palette replaces, omitted object preserves; one pending update with immediate replacement/cancellation
requirements.notes: Independent native scheduling/replacement/clear cases and presentation-state matrix. Fields omitted from a replacement are cleared rather than merged.

requirements.statement: apply using the current best clock estimate, even before convergence; optional easing
requirements.notes: Shared scheduled actor path and best-estimate/unavailability unit test; checked clock/deadline conversion prevents unrepresentable future timestamps from becoming immediate palettes. SDK publishes discrete state, not a color-blend renderer. This is not a physical audiovisual latency guarantee.

requirements.statement: required WCAG contrast for backgrounds/on-colors
requirements.notes: Palette generation/contrast adjustment is the server's duty. The SDK validates RGB shape/range and preserves values; it neither re-colors the palette nor certifies server extraction/contrast quality.

requirements.statement: role removal cancels palette state/pending updates; application owns returned slices
requirements.notes: Independent role removal/reactivation tests and defensive palette mutations in native/unit presentation tests. An empty applied palette is different from a removed role's nil state.

requirements.statement: 1–4 positional channels; omitted indices count as none; disabled channels receive no data
requirements.notes: Config/state validation, native multi-channel tests and `TestReferenceAllDisabledArtworkStreamStaysActiveWithoutImages`. Empty server channels for an all-disabled declaration do not end its stream.

requirements.statement: JPEG/PNG, exact dimensions, aspect ratio, black padding, no crop
requirements.notes: Existing native PNG/JPEG hashes, Go image decoding and padding checks are interoperability evidence. Encoding/scaling is server-owned; the SDK exposes encoded bytes rather than a renderer.

requirements.statement: stream channels match the current declaration; positional array never longer than four
requirements.notes: `TestArtworkStreamDeclarationAndResourceBounds`, independent malformed configuration E2E and identical-config preservation. Static declaration only; see AW10.

requirements.statement: exact headers/flags and 65519-byte per-message cap
requirements.notes: Unit boundary/malformed matrix and encrypted wire faults, including a logical over-cap message. Zero-byte parts are not independently forbidden by RC1. Announce-first transfer semantics and the absence of encoded image bytes in an announce are explicitly covered by the exact 14-byte announce and malformed extra-byte tests; only subsequent parts contribute image payload.

requirements.statement: one in-flight image across all channels; same-channel parts cannot overrun; cancel before replacement/end
requirements.notes: Cross-channel/overlap/overrun tests and `TestReferenceInFlightArtworkCancellationReplacementAndRemoval`. Real native cancel precedes replacement/end; missing cancel closes silently.

requirements.statement: active role/stream; unavailable discard still processes announces/cancels and counts all bytes
requirements.notes: Both-availability malformed matrix and `TestDiscardedArtworkStillAccountsForEveryPart`. A partly discarded image stays discarded after availability returns.

requirements.statement: per-channel current/pending state; announce replaces pending; cancel preserves current
requirements.notes: `TestArtworkCancellationIsPerChannelAndPreservesCurrent`, native scheduled and in-flight replacement/cancel tests, and same-direction partial-transfer markers.

requirements.statement: only complete due images; current best clock estimate without convergence wait; never drop for lateness
requirements.notes: `TestArtworkPendingUsesBestEstimateBeforeClockConvergence`; native replacement is deliberately past-timestamped and compared to the independent encoded hash/size. Shared checked clock/deadline conversion rejects unrepresentable future mappings instead of displaying immediately. Physical UI/clock-map bounds remain open.

requirements.statement: scheduled empty clear; stream end/role removal clears displayed and pending data
requirements.notes: Native empty-image scheduling, end/resume and mid-transfer removal; defensive/full-notification-buffer/concurrent read-model tests.

requirements.statement: runtime channel reconfiguration and clearing before disabling
requirements.notes: Config.Artwork is immutable for a Client; no live layout setter is offered. Different peer configurations are rejected. Optional runtime-layout support and sender clear-before-none/re-send behavior are not claimed from static tests.

requirements.statement: encoded total_size and local resource bounds
requirements.notes: Announce checks Config.MaxMessageBytes without eager payload allocation. The local encoded-image limit is not advertised as an artwork budget or a wire grammar limit; otherwise-valid large images can exceed it. Current/pending/event/caller copies add memory costs.

requirements.statement: late-join snapshots, paced parts, sensible lead; optional easing
requirements.notes: Native FIFO/packer/cancel logic stays unchanged in tests. Concurrent-audio pacing and every late-join current-then-scheduled replay remain unmeasured. SDK output is discrete encoded images, not cross-fades or validation of arbitrary image contents/geometry.

requirements.statement: fixed buffer capacity in hello; requested types/rate/spectrum in full client state
requirements.notes: Config validation/copying and native initial-state acceptance. Explicit empty requested types are supported. Rate is positive in the client's declaration; a supplied optional spectrum is validated even when unused. No live request setter is offered.

requirements.statement: echoed types subset, bounded rate, conditional beat/spectrum fields, matching complete spectrum
requirements.notes: `decodeVisualizerStream`, schema unit/fuzz matrix and `TestReferenceVisualizerStreamConditionalSchemaClosesSilently`. All spectrum keys are required, including a zero-valued f_min. Conditional fields must be absent without their type. Duplicate echo entries are accepted but normalized to a bounded effective set so redundant peer input cannot enlarge every frame lookup.

requirements.statement: active role/stream, one exact frame per message, big-endian data
requirements.notes: Per-type length/value matrix and independent malformed payload E2E. Known-but-unstreamed types are rejected before stale/unavailable discard. Empty negotiated types leave the stream active but allow no known visualization payloads.

requirements.statement: global non-decreasing timestamps across types; equality allowed; in-place update is not a reset
requirements.notes: `TestVisualizerOrderingDiscardCapacityAndStreamBoundaries`, native duplicate/reduced echo and decreasing-timestamp fault after an update. Configuration updates retain queued decoded data.

requirements.statement: clear releases buffered data and order cursor; end/removal also ends output
requirements.notes: Native clear/end/role-removal future-frame tests and unit queue/byte/reset checks. A new stream or clear allows lower timestamps; unchanged live stream updates do not. Re-handshake does not intentionally reset stream state; dedicated visualization/re-handshake stress remains useful. Final atomic review citation correction: the historical end/removal prose needs concrete core references in addition to role clear/reset text.

requirements.statement: unavailable clients discard valid data; past-on-arrival data is not rendered
requirements.notes: Native stale frame reception is proven by the transport observer, followed by a visualization-event FIFO barrier proving no stale event was emitted. Unavailable unit tests still enforce schema/order and release due bytes. Shared checked clock/deadline conversion rejects unrepresentable mappings rather than emitting at an invented immediate deadline; clock-map uncertainty and physical application latency remain unmeasured.

requirements.statement: beat reserved bits ignored by client; downbeat only with advertised tracker capability
requirements.notes: All 256 flag-byte combinations are checked in units, plus a real reference-packed 0xfe beat. Reserved high bits cannot change the public downbeat/strength/values. A low downbeat bit without capability is a peer protocol error.

requirements.statement: f_peak zero frequency requires zero amplitude; full uint16/byte domains and configured spectrum bin count
requirements.notes: Unit and independent wire value/size/invariant checks; all five native packed message types already compared to SDK events. A-weighting, dB/frequency bin generation, beat accuracy and onset analysis are server duties, not certified by receiver byte equivalence.

requirements.statement: do not implement reserved sender IDs 21–23; receiver ignores unimplemented IDs after activation
requirements.notes: Native raw reserved IDs are authenticated/received and ignored even after stream end, without reopening the role or producing a visualization. This does not excuse a current-spec sender using them; generic fragment-sequence validation still applies. Final atomic review citation correction: the historical receiver ignore rule needs the core citation in addition to the reserved sender-ID prohibition.

requirements.statement: byte capacity counts reassembled type/timestamp/data; clear/end reset
requirements.notes: Local queue size/count equality is checked in unit/stateful fuzz tests, including exact-fit and over-cap behavior. The SDK's local future-time accounting is not the server-clock ledger and cannot certify sender compliance under mapping uncertainty. No universal renderer/event-memory budget is claimed.

requirements.statement: periodic per-type rate vs event-driven beat/peak and analysis scaling
requirements.notes: The SDK neither caps all types together nor derives tempo/FFT/onsets itself. Native vectors and beat schedules exercise transport, not periodic-rate measurements, HTK/log bin algorithms or musical quality. Final atomic review citation correction: frequency-bin mapping formula is in this field, not the periodic-rate or bin-size-limit bullets.

requirements.statement: queued values are decoded at receipt and application-owned on delivery
requirements.notes: `TestVisualizerEventsOwnValuesAndUnavailableDrainReleasesBytes` checks frame-buffer independence, distinct event slices, due-byte release and unavailable suppression. Delivery is bounded best-effort, not a hardware-timed/lossless rendering channel; GUI backpressure/latency remain application responsibilities.

requirements.statement: implement Pairing PSK; other methods optional; prefer dynamic over static code when offering a code method
requirements.notes: The frozen baseline/default Client profile advertises only pairing_psk. At explicit user request the SDK now also implements opt-in static/dynamic PIN profiles, one code method per Client. Their extension tests do not promote the frozen PSK-only primary assessments or constitute independent cryptographic/product acceptance; see docs/pin-pairing.md.

requirements.statement: unique long-lived CSPRNG pairing PSK, not consumed by success; expose a token with the client key
requirements.notes: `NewCredentials`, `Credentials.PairingToken`; token vector, persistence and independent repair/multi-server pairing tests. Successful pairing produces a distinct long-term key, without replacing identity/pairing PSK.

requirements.statement: pairing PSK always a candidate; verify matched PSK before any pair-init
requirements.notes: Resolver and activation method/category guard; native repair, both-suite E2E and refusal matrix. Pairing protection is linearized before first transmission, not after Write/observation returns (`TestReferencePairingProtectionStartsBeforeFirstWriteReturns`); a previously decided handoff prevents late pair-init (`TestDecidedDisplacementPreventsALatePairInit`). A refusal discloses neither pair-init nor finalize.

requirements.statement: PSK pair-init then immediate direct-PSK finalize; persist only after server finalize
requirements.notes: Serialized activation handler; native reference pairing, `TestReferencePSKPairingIgnoresUnknownParameterFields`, and paused-Store fault tests. No PAKE fields are emitted. The reference's sequence/index validators remain enabled.

requirements.statement: persist a new key bound to server identity, replacing an old record for that identity
requirements.notes: Atomic Store snapshot update; independent client/server credential-loss and repair scenarios, `TestPairingCompletionReleasesAttemptProtection`. Failed/cancelled pending exchanges persist nothing locally. The lifecycle overview also describes shared persistence and server promotion; only the client's bound-record transaction is implemented here. The peer's persistence/transition duties are separately R16-R18 and CN25.

requirements.statement: at least five records; at capacity evict only an unused record; cap open connections below capacity
requirements.notes: Config minimum, protected selection and native full-store pairing with three gated record-backed handshakes; only the oldest unused record is evicted. Pending pr/sn rekey selection retains long-term protection until key commit. Both outgoing post-upgrade and incoming ServeHTTP pr-rekey write faults check binding during the blocked/failed response and after error: zero/partial/full-carrier errors, cancellation and deadline retain the old binding through teardown. New-key state failure after successful commit remains distinct. Inbound mode reservation is also verified/released. These net.Conn simulations do not replace native OS/load or real storage-failure evidence.

requirements.statement: pairing activity alone preserves roles/streams/group; locally suspend only a shared dynamic-code output
requirements.notes: PSK pairing uses no code out-channel. Native buffered rekey/pairing evidence now proves stream/queued-data retention; exact complete-role-set and group-membership continuity remain narrower atomic proof gaps. Code-output suspension/availability/discard/resume duties are explicitly conditional on the unselected code-method MAY, not claimed as implemented.

requirements.statement: bounded attempt from first client message; on expiry abort with attempt_timeout
requirements.notes: Two-minute deadline checked by timer and before disclosure/finalize acceptance/transaction entry. This atomic review reproduced a missing attempt deadline on context-cooperative Store.Save, fixed it and added a real post-peer-commit/no-actor-ticker expiry regression. Parent/store-owned earlier timeouts are not invented attempt expiries. Arbitrary blocking callbacks, mutex/native I/O and uncertain custom-store commits remain outside the finite bound; no general hard-real-time or distributed rollback claim follows.

requirements.statement: a cancelling activation abandons pending pairing without persistence; discard only until the next activation
requirements.notes: `TestNextActivationEndsPairingDiscardWindow`, `TestRemoteAbortAbandonsPendingPairingWithoutPersistence`; independent stale-message-before-native-cancellation / invalid-finalize-after-barrier test. The same-direction ordering is essential: a later finalize cannot be a leftover.

requirements.statement: pairing message sequencing and pairing_index count since last Noise handshake
requirements.notes: Recognized PSK-inapplicable/wrong-direction messages fail outside the discard window; native first/re-handshake rejection and successful retry both observe index 2. Re-pairing the same promoted connection observes indices 1, then 1 after re-handshake. Counter overflow closes rather than wraps (`TestPairingIndexCannotWrap`).

requirements.statement: malformed/missing fields and out-of-sequence messages close silently and persist nothing
requirements.notes: Independent malformed activation, code-message mid-PSK and general protocol fault E2E; unit shape matrix. Detection is local: a remote Store operation already in progress may commit after socket closure, without the SDK ever acknowledging/persisting its key.

requirements.statement: non-closing abort leaves socket open; after own attempt ended, a late abort has no effect
requirements.notes: `TestAbortAfterCompletedAttemptHasNoEffect`, remote-abort unit test and native refusal/retry E2E. Invalid client-only abort reasons from the server remain protocol errors during a live attempt. Concurrent-attempt closure is independently covered by arbitration E2E. The full reason list now includes user_cancelled through its actual final source line. Live attempts reject server use of client-only reasons and malformed known reason values without writes; after own completion the late-abort no-op exception still applies.

requirements.statement: manufacturer's unpaired-access choice; closing when it is withdrawn; server approval and MITM caveat
requirements.notes: Disabled by default and immutable for each Client; native repair/refusal tests show no unpaired bypass. No runtime toggle is offered. Server-side approval/UI/persistence is S; Sentinel encryption alone authenticates no peer identity.

requirements.statement: versioned pairing token encoding/lenient decoding; reject malformed/short payload and ignore reserved trailing bytes
requirements.notes: Frozen vector, optional/mixed-case prefix, surrounding whitespace, original/transliterated alphabet, partial/full padding and reserved-extension matrix. Malformed ASCII/Unicode/embedded-line-break cases return no partial credentials; `FuzzPairingToken` checks canonical roundtrip ownership. This is deliberately more lenient than wire Base64URL. Version-1 code tokens remain outside this PSK-only parser. The version-0 payload is exactly the 32-byte client public key followed by the 32-byte pairing PSK; the pinned vector tests this layout separately from general lenient operator decoding. Extra bytes remain reserved, not an alternate credential layout.

requirements.statement: code derivation, windows/rounds, PAKE/wrapping, code-method descriptors
requirements.notes: No dynamic/static code method is advertised, so client code-flow obligations do not apply. The PSK descriptor is `{}`; optional location hints/printed QR packaging belong to the embedding product. Server selection/unknown descriptor rules are S. The pending/auth/confirm/retry/nonce/commit/wrapped fields in these code-only message definitions were reviewed as deliberately unoffered flow scope, not implemented or silently accepted. Shared PSK pair-init/index/finalize/abort obligations remain separately R03-R12. Recognized code-only messages still fail out of sequence unless the explicit stale-message discard window applies.

requirements.statement: Before selecting PSK pairing on a Sentinel/long-term session, re-handshake to the device's pairing PSK
requirements.notes: The server initiates this key transition; the client continuously retains its pairing PSK candidate and verifies method/category before revealing a new key (R03). Successful native re-pairing exercises one server implementation but is not a universal server policy certification.

requirements.statement: End a pairing transition with an activation declaring the resulting activities and active roles
requirements.notes: Server sender duty. The client applies the subsequent activation under its newly matched key and preserves/removes roles according to M15-M17 and CN25. The client must not manufacture its own resulting role/priority declaration after success or timeout.

requirements.statement: Persist the long-term pairing PSK bound to the client's authenticated client_id
requirements.notes: The SDK is a client and persists its counterpart server_id binding. A native peer's actual post-persistence finalize is interoperability evidence, not an implementation of a server trust store or proof of every remote failure/rollback behavior.

obligations.statement: Initialize output_delay_ms to zero when no persisted value exists.
obligations.condition: New player credentials without a prior delay
obligations.notes: Default-value field contract; native first mute echo observes zero delay before any delay setter. Not a physical port-latency measurement.

obligations.statement: Clamp output_delay_ms to 0..5000 before applying it.
obligations.condition: A local or remote delay value is supplied
obligations.notes: The remote int64-extreme cases assert exact clamped state and one Store transaction; the local duration setter clamps before conversion.

obligations.statement: Retain the local output-delay value across client restart and server reconnection.
obligations.condition: A player has persisted output_delay_ms
obligations.notes: The FileStore/native test sets 123 ms, recreates Client, checks retained state and reconnects with the existing pairing. Does not certify disk hardware durability.

obligations.statement: Optionally change output_delay_ms and supported_commands when the output changes.
obligations.condition: Runtime hardware-output switching policy is selected
obligations.notes: No automatic output-change detector or mutable command capability API is offered. This permission is not a mandatory SDK feature.

obligations.statement: Optionally persist a separate delay for each output.
obligations.condition: Per-output identity and settings are implemented
obligations.notes: The SDK persists one device setting; a per-output settings database is deliberately not implemented. Do not turn this MAY into a missing MUST.

obligations.statement: Remain operational during temporary buffered excess after a delay decrease.
obligations.condition: Previously sent audio temporarily exceeds the configured buffer cap
obligations.notes: Bounded reset accepts the fresh chunk instead of disconnecting on aggregate excess. This is operational software recovery, not an inaudible-recovery claim.

obligations.statement: Optionally drop buffered audio to recover at the new timeline.
obligations.condition: Temporary buffer excess requires recovery
obligations.notes: The SDK selects the permitted discard/reset policy. Its rarity and audible quality remain separate measurement obligations.

obligations.statement: Avoid audible interruption when recovering from temporary buffered excess.
obligations.condition: Delay-change buffer recovery occurs
obligations.notes: No loopback/listening evidence for delay-change recovery on real output exists. Passing the operational-overflow test does not satisfy this recommendation.

obligations.statement: Interpret output_delay_ms as delay beyond the audio port, not internal DAC/buffer processing delay.
obligations.condition: Interpreting timing and measurement results
obligations.notes: Definition used to distinguish configured external delay from Device.Next port timing. Numerical software scheduling is not a DAC-latency measurement.

obligations.statement: Optionally update required_lead_time_ms and min_buffer_ms at runtime.
obligations.condition: A runtime timing-parameter update API is selected
obligations.notes: Timing hints are immutable Config values for this SDK. Runtime setters are a permission, not an unconditional implementation gap.

obligations.statement: Optionally lower startup lead while a stream runs and raise it before the next stream.
obligations.condition: Dynamic startup-lead policy is implemented
obligations.notes: No dynamic warmup policy is offered; this is separate from the requirement to report valid nonnegative timing fields.

obligations.statement: Factor updated player timing hints into subsequent playback timing.
obligations.condition: A server receives updated timing values
obligations.notes: Sender timing policy belongs to the server. Do not assign this MUST to the receiving SDK or certify all servers from one interoperability run.

obligations.statement: Debounce measured timing changes before reporting sustained new parameters.
obligations.condition: Local measurements drive runtime timing updates
obligations.notes: Conditional SHOULD retained, not excluded under the timing-update MAY: debounce applies when measurements change reported hints. The selected SDK profile has immutable Config hints and no measurement-driven update path, so there are no such updates to debounce. This is a reviewed API/policy boundary, not tested estimator fulfillment. P08.05 still independently questions the derivation duty; adding an estimator or mutable hints must reopen this implementation/evidence review. See rc1-review-decisions.md.

obligations.statement: Determine the normative force of deriving min_buffer_ms from measured arrival-delay distribution.
