obligations.condition: Player timing-hint derivation
obligations.notes: The declarative derivation sentence precedes explicit SHOULD rules. The SDK has static application-chosen hints, not an arrival-delay estimator. Do not silently downgrade the declarative algorithm to MAY or assert a missing MUST without resolving this reading.

obligations.statement: Size min_buffer_ms from the upper tail of an arrival-delay window that includes intermittent interference.
obligations.condition: Selecting player buffering hints for expected conditions
obligations.notes: No upper-tail sampler/window estimator is implemented. Config input alone is not execution evidence for the recommended derivation; missing recommendation is distinct from an established mandatory protocol failure.

obligations.statement: Discard timing-estimator samples collected before clock convergence.
obligations.condition: Arrival-delay samples are collected for timing-parameter estimation
obligations.notes: Conditional SHOULD retained for an arrival-delay estimator, not turned into an optional exclusion. The current SDK collects no arrival-delay samples; therefore no preconvergence sample enters an estimator. Review closes only this trigger/applicability question, not the independent P08.05 derivation question or a future estimator's compliance. Adding sampling must reopen targeted evidence for discarding preconvergence and saturated send_ahead samples. See rc1-review-decisions.md.

obligations.statement: Report the lowest timing hints that reliably prevent underruns and startup truncation under expected conditions.
obligations.condition: Choosing required lead and minimum buffer for a deployment
obligations.notes: The SDK accepts explicit hints but no deployment/OS/backend calibration establishes minimum reliable latency. This is measurement/configuration evidence, not merely a missing setter.

obligations.statement: Factor expected network delay and jitter into both timing hints.
obligations.condition: Provisioning player hints for LAN, Wi-Fi or remote conditions
obligations.notes: No network/load campaign validates the chosen defaults for all deployments. Empirical hint calibration must not be confused with exact outgoing-field serialization.

obligations.statement: Never include output_delay_ms in required_lead_time_ms or min_buffer_ms.
obligations.condition: Reporting player timing hints
obligations.notes: The independent peer compares complete echoes with hints 35/20 unchanged while output delay ranges from 0 to 5000. This test does not measure whether those hints are optimal.

obligations.statement: Distinguish startup-trigger warmup from steady-state arrival delay when interpreting lead time.
obligations.condition: Designing a timing estimator or calibration plan
obligations.notes: The explanatory burst/start-trigger distinction is retained; one jitter statistic cannot by itself establish startup/DAC warmup. This is not an implemented estimator.

obligations.statement: Timestamp the first chunk of a new format immediately after the prior-format timeline.
obligations.condition: Changing an active player stream format
obligations.notes: The server owns timestamp continuity. SDK queue preservation cannot certify a remote sender's timeline policy.

obligations.statement: Do not resend audio already sent before an in-place format change.
obligations.condition: Changing an active player stream format
obligations.notes: Sender no-replay policy is distinct from cryptographic replay rejection and client buffer ownership.

obligations.statement: Retain already buffered chunks when the active stream format changes.
obligations.condition: An in-place player stream/start changes format
obligations.notes: The worker drains old-format queued values before opening the next device. Physical reopen gap and sender timestamp continuity remain separate obligations.

obligations.statement: Decode each chunk with the format in effect when that chunk was received.
obligations.condition: Old and new formats coexist in the playback queue
obligations.notes: A combined receive/decode/enqueue/render trace buffers built-in PCM16, real encoded FLAC and PCM24, switches the live decoder again before rendering, and compares exact old/new samples. Another all-role in-place update retains queued PCM24 while receiving new stereo PCM16. Virtual output only; not hardware gaplessness.

obligations.statement: Advertise only one rate/channel layout when the output cannot switch advertised layouts without a gap.
obligations.condition: Advertising formats across output layouts with non-gapless transitions
obligations.notes: Defaults already use a single 48-kHz stereo layout. Multi-layout Config/backend transitions still need physical characterization; a successful Close/Open sequence is not proof of gaplessness.

obligations.statement: Clear all buffered player audio when stream/clear targets player.
obligations.condition: A valid player stream/clear is received
obligations.notes: A gated old write and a following decoded chunk are discarded before fresh output; software-only flush does not establish physical downstream stop latency.

obligations.statement: Continue the active player stream using chunks received after stream/clear.
obligations.condition: Fresh audio follows a valid player clear
obligations.notes: The clear case asserts that the stream stays active and only the fresh marker reaches the retained output.

obligations.statement: Do not send audio outside an active player stream.
obligations.condition: Sending player audio
obligations.notes: Server sender duty; the SDK's rejection of invalid no-stream audio is defensive receive behavior, not an implementation of that sender.

obligations.statement: Discard otherwise valid player audio while locally unavailable.
obligations.condition: Valid audio arrives on an active stream while unavailable
obligations.notes: Independent native encrypted valid PCM is observed twice while unavailable, followed by a same-direction marker. No output opens or decoded-delivery callbacks occur; availability recovery accepts only the fresh distinct sample marker, never the discarded values.

obligations.statement: Do not close solely because valid audio arrives while locally unavailable.
obligations.condition: Valid audio arrives on an active unavailable player stream
obligations.notes: The native test explicitly observes the still-open connection and active player stream after valid unavailable data, processes following group markers, and resumes fresh audio. Crossed-lifecycle input is deliberately injected; it is not a claim that a server normally starts from a reported unavailable state.

obligations.statement: Interpret the player binary header as ID 4, a big-endian int64 timestamp and a big-endian uint32 send_ahead.
obligations.condition: Receiving a player audio chunk
obligations.notes: One packet-layout predicate from the field definition, not an extra transport capability. The harness compares actual header/source observations; physical playout timing is separate.

obligations.statement: Translate the server audio timestamp using the required time-filter mapping.
obligations.condition: Scheduling player audio
obligations.notes: This is the required software clock translation, including checked representability. Applying the algorithm does not establish actual audio-port accuracy.

obligations.statement: Subtract configured output_delay_ms from server timestamps before scheduling player audio.
obligations.condition: Mapping a player audio deadline
obligations.notes: The repeated clause is one shared obligation, not two fulfillment counts. Tests cover exact subtraction, int64 saturation and a changed delay during waiting; no physical timing claim follows.

obligations.statement: Account for known internal processing/DAC/buffer delay when submitting audio to hardware.
obligations.condition: A backend has known downstream processing delays
obligations.notes: Device.Next specifies port timing and the purego native backends account for reported native clocks/queues. Actual latency compensation remains physically unmeasured; replacing the removed Oto/PortAudio adapters does not promote this hardware assessment.

obligations.statement: Send send_ahead=0 when transmission is at or after the audio timestamp.
obligations.condition: Encoding a player chunk whose true lead is nonpositive
obligations.notes: Sender saturation is distinct from receiving/diagnostically exposing the field; the SDK does not produce server audio chunks.

obligations.statement: Send send_ahead=4294967295 when true lead exceeds the uint32 range.
obligations.condition: Encoding a player chunk whose true lead exceeds uint32
obligations.notes: A separate sender upper-saturation condition; not a client arithmetic implementation requirement.

obligations.statement: Never use chunks with either saturated send_ahead value as measured arrival-delay samples.
obligations.condition: Considering send_ahead for a delay estimator
obligations.notes: The currently non-estimating path is tested metamorphically at zero, one, an interior lead, MaxUint32-1 and MaxUint32. Clock mapping/error and scheduled/output values remain identical. This guards the no-sampling/current-profile boundary; a future estimator must add its own sample-ledger tests, not inherit this result.

obligations.statement: Do not let send_ahead change when an audio chunk is scheduled.
obligations.condition: Scheduling a chunk with any send_ahead value
obligations.notes: Changing only send_ahead leaves the exact timestamp supplied to the worker clock mapper and all submitted samples unchanged, including both saturated values. No physical scheduling accuracy is inferred from the virtual device.

obligations.statement: Drop late audio to maintain synchronization.
obligations.condition: Chunks or their leading samples are already late
obligations.notes: The explicit level is SHOULD. Whole expired chunks and saturated old deadlines are discarded; rare resync and physical output accuracy remain separate requirements.

obligations.statement: Do not produce audible noise, warble or distortion from individual steady-state corrections.
obligations.condition: Normal steady-state listening
obligations.notes: Requires defined signal/listening/loopback conditions across real backends. Discrete frame edits and small numeric steps alone cannot demonstrate inaudibility.

obligations.statement: Keep effective steady-state playback speed within +/-0.5% over every sliding 150-ms window.
obligations.condition: Continuous steady-state correction, excluding permitted discrete resync
obligations.notes: Linked tests bound absolute edits on a predicted output timeline. Their passes are software evidence only; actual device speed/clock behavior still needs measurement, so this atom remains partial.

obligations.statement: Keep discrete one-shot resynchronizations rare.
obligations.condition: Recovery from startup, underrun or an error too large for smooth correction
obligations.notes: The speed-cap exemption does not waive the separate rarity duty. Define representative disturbances/load and an operational interpretation of rare before collecting sustained resync measurements.

obligations.statement: Measure sync error at the audio output relative to the time-filter prediction and configured external delay, not the true server clock.
obligations.condition: Defining physical sync measurements
obligations.notes: Measurement definition and allocation of each client's responsibility. The concrete floor/target are separate normative atoms; this definition is not an accuracy pass.

obligations.statement: Keep physical steady-state audio-output error within +/-1 ms.
obligations.condition: Steady state outside rare exempt one-shot resynchronizations
obligations.notes: No physical audio-port measurement establishes this bound. Algorithm parity, fake Device.Next timing, native builds and approximate Oto smoke tests cannot satisfy it.

obligations.statement: Aim for physical sync error within +/-0.5 ms.
obligations.condition: Steady-state player output
obligations.notes: This recommendation is distinct from the mandatory 1-ms floor; both require real output measurements rather than a single aggregate parent verdict.

obligations.statement: Do not produce audible pitch modulation, warble or other startup artifacts.
obligations.condition: Startup of player output
obligations.notes: One-shot alignment and gain ramps exist, but startup signal quality has not been measured/listened to on native platforms/backends.

obligations.statement: Treat the suggested drop/duplicate correction strategy as a nonbinding implementation example.
obligations.condition: Choosing a correction strategy
obligations.notes: The SDK uses a related discrete strategy, but sample-step/dead-band examples are not independent conformance duties. The binding rare-resync reminder at line 188 remains explicitly mapped to P17.02.

obligations.statement: Prefer server-initiated connections for standardized multi-server behavior.
obligations.condition: The embedding application chooses a connection strategy
obligations.notes: The library offers and documents Serve/advertising as well as explicit outbound APIs; the host chooses the strategy. The recommendation is not a requirement to remove client-initiated support or force a default connection in a library.

obligations.statement: Support both standard connection methods on the server.
obligations.condition: Implementing a Sendspin server
obligations.notes: This SDK is the client, including when it accepts the WebSocket. WebSocket server role must not be confused with Sendspin server duties.

obligations.statement: Use only one connection method at a time, advertising or discovering accordingly.
obligations.condition: Running a standard Sendspin connection/discovery mode
obligations.notes: The isolated real-discovery test verifies mode reservation and rejects the conflicting direction. Native OS/interface-switching stress remains separate scope.

obligations.statement: Do not manually connect outbound while advertising the client service.
obligations.condition: The client service advertisement is active
obligations.notes: Direction reservation covers the discovery lifetime, not just an already-admitted WebSocket.

obligations.statement: Do not advertise the client service while using client-initiated connections.
obligations.condition: Outbound discovery/connect mode is reserved
obligations.notes: Separate direction of the exclusion rule; it does not assert scoped IPv6 or native interface-change behavior.

obligations.statement: Optionally admit a pairing connection alongside a playback holder.
obligations.condition: Selecting the optional two-holder pairing policy
obligations.notes: The SDK deliberately selects the permitted single-holder policy. This explicit unselected MAY is the applicability parent for the two-holder-only duties below.

obligations.statement: Refuse incoming pairing with pair/abort concurrent_attempt when it is not admitted alongside playback.
obligations.condition: A pairing candidate arrives while the single playback holder remains admitted
obligations.notes: The native API observes the exact refusal reason and the unchanged playback holder. Optional parallel admission does not waive this alternative-path duty.

obligations.statement: Close the incoming pairing connection after its single-holder policy refusal.
obligations.condition: Incoming pairing is refused rather than admitted alongside playback
obligations.notes: After native concurrent_attempt refusal, the test now waits for the peer disconnected state and SDK slot/mode release without forcing the candidate closed, then verifies the holder through a fresh same-direction barrier.

obligations.statement: Arbitrate further incoming connections against the playback holder while two connections are held.
obligations.condition: The optional parallel pairing policy holds two connections
obligations.notes: A conditional MUST inside an explicitly unselected MAY branch, not a blanket optional label for an unconditional obligation. No two-holder state is implemented.

obligations.statement: Re-arbitrate the former parallel pairing connection as incoming when its pairing activity ends.
obligations.condition: An optionally co-admitted pairing connection drops pairing
obligations.notes: The alternative-path transition remains normative if parallel admission is ever added. It is not a current single-holder implementation bug.

obligations.statement: Optionally cap concurrently held provisional connections.
obligations.condition: Selecting a bounded session resource policy
obligations.notes: The SDK chooses a bounded total-session cap. This proves enforcement/recovery, not every mandated reason or authenticated refusal path.

obligations.statement: Resolve whether pre-Noise capacity closure satisfies rejecting excess peers as lower priority.
obligations.condition: The selected session cap rejects a new connection before authentication
obligations.notes: The current cap closes before Noise, so no encrypted concurrent_attempt reason is available. Reconcile the lower-priority wording with the reason/closure rules in C:42 before declaring a code defect or compliant exception. Existing cap-pass evidence alone does not resolve it.

obligations.statement: Keep the number of open paired connections below record capacity so an evictable record exists.
obligations.condition: Opening SDK sessions with bounded pairing-record storage
obligations.notes: The configured minimum is five and the cap is at most four total sessions. The native boundary test actually has four open sessions with five stored records.

obligations.statement: Do not evict a pairing record backing an open provisional or admitted connection.
obligations.condition: Pairing completes at record capacity
obligations.notes: Native initial-handshake barriers and the pending-rekey/commit regression cover when protection starts and when the old binding may be released. No storage-device fault durability claim follows.

obligations.statement: Evict an unused record rather than fail successful pairing solely for record capacity.
obligations.condition: Pairing completes with a full record store
obligations.notes: The full-store test verifies one successful Save and eviction of only the oldest unprotected record. An actual disk/Store I/O error is not a capacity-policy failure.

obligations.statement: Use the end-to-end KKpsk2 Noise pattern for Sendspin connections.
obligations.condition: Establishing a Sendspin channel
obligations.notes: Interoperability checks the configured pattern and PSK placement, not an independent proof of the underlying cryptographic construction.

obligations.statement: Act as Noise responder regardless of which side initiated the WebSocket.
obligations.condition: Initial handshake or re-handshake in either WebSocket direction
obligations.notes: The peer independently initiates both Noise exchanges and decrypts the client's response in both WebSocket roles, using the shared Noise primitive.

obligations.statement: Reject replayed or out-of-order transport ciphertext and abort the connection.
obligations.condition: An invalid transport-counter ciphertext arrives
obligations.notes: Both suites and both actual public connection directions reject a repeated authenticated carrier and an out-of-order carrier with actual handler closure, no further application reply, unchanged trust and released session/admission/mode state. This is not independent primitive/forward-secrecy proof.

obligations.statement: Provide the stated transport forward-secrecy property, with the specified first-handshake-payload exception.
obligations.condition: Assessing compromise of static keys or PSK after a session
obligations.notes: C:74 is a mandatory declarative transport security contract, not a new cipher requirement. The pinned primitive/SDK source review is now recorded in cryptographic-review.md: ephemeral DH, explicit OS CSPRNG responder configuration, key/counter ownership, rekey commit, secret persistence and message-1 exception. New source-policy guards are not independent crypto proof. External/independent assurance is not claimed, so this C/review row deliberately remains a mandatory blocker rather than being promoted by source inspection, interop or network-load passes.

obligations.statement: Hash exact raw client/init followed by raw server/init bytes as the initial prologue.
obligations.condition: Constructing the initial Noise transcript
obligations.notes: The independent framing script changes whitespace/key order and unknown fields and completes the exchange only with the exact raw-byte prologue.

obligations.statement: Use raw init bytes rather than re-encoding them when the server builds its prologue.
obligations.condition: Constructing the initial Noise transcript
obligations.notes: The same both-sides clause creates a separate server duty; the SDK's client prologue test does not certify every remote implementation.

obligations.statement: Send the matching server/error reason in place of server/init for a cleartext client-init failure.
obligations.condition: Rejecting client/init before Noise
obligations.notes: Server emission is not a client feature. Receiving an unauthenticated reason is only a refusal/logging hint, not proof it is true.

obligations.statement: Close the connection after sending an init-failure server/error.
obligations.condition: The server has rejected client/init
obligations.notes: Separate sender closure duty; client-side safe refusal of both valid and invalid hint bodies is not evidence for this server action.

obligations.statement: Apply unsupported-version precedence, then suite, then remaining init-shape checks when selecting a server/error reason.
obligations.condition: Classifying a cleartext client/init failure
obligations.notes: Normative ordering algorithm despite the absence of another uppercase MUST in this paragraph. It must not become an optional client-side reason validator.

obligations.statement: Close silently, without additional application data, on non-init client-side handshake or transport failure.
obligations.condition: Detecting malformed handshake, timeout, failed authentication, forbidden cleartext or lookup miss without fallback
obligations.notes: The peer checks actual closure/no later data and unchanged trust; WebSocket control-close frames are not application replies. Finite software paths do not claim all native cancellation/load races.

obligations.statement: Apply receive timeouts to expected init and Noise-handshake phases.
obligations.condition: Waiting for the next expected handshake/activation message
obligations.notes: The SDK uses an aggregate initial activation budget, capped at 30 seconds, and a rekey timeout. This is stricter than restarting a full budget per message, not a hard real-time guarantee for arbitrary blocking callbacks or native calls.

obligations.statement: Optionally initiate an in-band Noise re-handshake to swap session keys.
obligations.condition: The server chooses promotion or rotation on an open connection
obligations.notes: The peer's permission does not mean a client may ignore a valid rekey. The participating client duties are separately classified below.

obligations.statement: Send client Noise message 2 as encrypted JSON under the pre-rekey transport keys.
obligations.condition: Responding to an in-band re-handshake
obligations.notes: The scripted peer decrypts the response under old keys and validates its literal inner empty object before installing new states, in both WebSocket directions.

obligations.statement: Carry client_id, server_id and suite across rekey without sending a new client/init.
obligations.condition: Re-handshaking the same WebSocket connection
obligations.notes: The peer runs the same identity/suite and accepts only old-key clock requests or Noise response before activation; no fresh init exchange is admitted.

obligations.statement: Use the prior handshake hash as the new handshake's prologue.
obligations.condition: Starting an in-band re-handshake
obligations.notes: The positive prior-hash exchange and wrong-prologue negative case are separate controls; they share the Noise primitive, not SDK transcript construction.

obligations.statement: Send server/activate as the first new-key server message.
obligations.condition: New rekey transport keys have been installed
obligations.notes: The server's ordered send duty is distinct from the client's tested enforcement of its receive gate.

obligations.statement: Do not start new client application messages between receiving Noise message 1 and the new activation.
obligations.condition: The in-band re-handshake quiet period is active
obligations.notes: Actor, request and shutdown paths keep the write gate; valid old-key requests sent before receipt may already be in flight and are not violations.

obligations.statement: Do not re-send client/hello during an in-band re-handshake.
obligations.condition: The connection has already exchanged its initial hello
obligations.notes: The peer expects a clock request, not another hello, after valid new-key activation. The initial hello remains connection-wide state.

obligations.statement: Apply subsequent-activation and omitted-role rules under the newly matched PSK.
obligations.condition: Receiving activation after an in-band re-handshake
obligations.notes: Actual rekeys to lt/pr/sn test omitted and explicit roles under both local access policies. Further activity/method cases independently assert paired pairing prohibition, pairing_required versus unauthorized precedence, method mismatch, allowed pairing and authorized playback under the newly installed category.

obligations.statement: Do not start new server application messages after sending Noise message 1 until sending new activation.
obligations.condition: Server in-band re-handshake quiet period
obligations.notes: Receiver fault rejection does not implement the remote server's quiet-period policy.

obligations.statement: Do not re-send server/init or server/hello as part of an in-band re-handshake.
obligations.condition: Rekeying an established WebSocket
obligations.notes: A server sequencing duty, separate from the SDK's rejection of duplicate hello/init messages.

obligations.statement: Do not send an audio chunk longer than 150 ms.
obligations.condition: Sending player audio chunks
obligations.notes: Sender maximum duration. Defensive SDK decoder length limits are not proof of every remote server's compliance.

obligations.statement: Avoid chunks shorter than 15 ms except at stream end or before a format change.
obligations.condition: Sending a non-final chunk outside a format-change boundary
obligations.notes: The source exceptions are conditions on the recommendation, not unconditional permission for arbitrary small chunks.

obligations.statement: Use future audio timestamps when starting a late-joining client.
obligations.condition: Adding a player to ongoing playback
obligations.notes: Declarative server send contract; receiving late audio defensively does not implement the remote late-join scheduler.

obligations.statement: Schedule the first audio timestamp far enough ahead to satisfy startup send-ahead after empty-buffer start or clear.
obligations.condition: Starting from empty or after player stream/clear
obligations.notes: Live playback cannot accumulate startup headroom after output begins; the server must establish it before the first chunk.

obligations.statement: Do not reapply startup lead on an in-place active-stream configuration update.
obligations.condition: Sending stream/start for an already active timeline
obligations.notes: Distinguishes configuration update from empty-buffer startup; preserving SDK queued audio is only the client counterpart.

obligations.statement: Factor each player's output delay separately into server send-ahead.
obligations.condition: Computing audio send-ahead headroom
obligations.notes: This is separate from the client's MUST NOT to add external output delay to its reported timing hints.

obligations.statement: Schedule initial audio at least min_buffer_ms plus output_delay_ms ahead.
obligations.condition: Computing the first-chunk lead
obligations.notes: The required lead hint is not a replacement for the specified minimum sum.

obligations.statement: Extend lead toward required_lead_time_ms only when that adds no latency.
obligations.condition: A buffered source permits extending startup lead without latency cost
obligations.notes: The recommendation is conditioned on no added latency and does not authorize treating buffered/live sources identically.

obligations.statement: Use the maximum per-player send-ahead as the group's common send-ahead.
obligations.condition: Scheduling grouped playback
obligations.notes: A server grouping algorithm, not a client-side estimate of other speakers.

obligations.statement: Recompute group send-ahead when players join, leave or update timing parameters.
obligations.condition: Group membership or player timing changes
obligations.notes: The update trigger is distinct from the maximum selection formula.

obligations.statement: Optionally retain or reduce common send-ahead when its maximum decreases.
obligations.condition: A group/timing update lowers the maximum required send-ahead
obligations.notes: An explicit server policy choice between latency and continuity; not a missing SDK setter.

obligations.statement: Keep each live player's queued duration at least its requested minimum, subject to the hard byte cap.
obligations.condition: Scheduling live audio within buffer_capacity constraints
obligations.notes: The encoded byte-rate/cap exception is part of the condition, not permission for a client to invent a buffering ACK protocol.

obligations.statement: Optionally fall temporarily below requested min_buffer_ms when timing/group updates increase required live send-ahead.
obligations.condition: Live send-ahead increases during playback
obligations.notes: This client permission was hidden inside the historical server-only aggregate. It is an allowed temporary state, not a mandatory feature or a requirement that the SDK reject insufficient buffering.

obligations.statement: Restore requested live minimum buffering after increased send-ahead, subject to capacity.
obligations.condition: An update temporarily reduces live buffer headroom
obligations.notes: The restoration recommendation belongs to the sender, unlike the adjacent player MAY.

obligations.statement: Prefer filling buffered-source player queues near buffer_capacity.
obligations.condition: Serving a buffered source
obligations.notes: The imperative prefer is a recommendation rather than a new mandatory full-buffer rule.

obligations.statement: Do not begin sending a chunk if its full size plus current outstanding count exceeds buffer_capacity.
obligations.condition: Admitting another encoded audio chunk to the send ledger
obligations.notes: One shared hard byte-cap predicate, not two pass counts. SDK memory-limit recovery is defensive and is not this exact server ledger.

obligations.statement: Optionally rate-limit, debounce or coalesce player timing updates.
obligations.condition: Handling frequent or small client timing updates
obligations.notes: A sender permission, distinct from the client's measurement-debounce SHOULD.

obligations.statement: Count only each chunk's 13-byte header and encoded payload in outstanding-byte accounting.
obligations.condition: Updating the player buffer ledger
obligations.notes: Does not count decoded float buffers, AEAD tags or WebSocket overhead; those may still need separate defensive memory bounds in the client.

obligations.statement: Count a chunk in full while its send is unfinished or its completion lies in the future, regardless of partial playback/discard.
obligations.condition: Deciding whether an already sent chunk remains outstanding
obligations.notes: A server-clock completion predicate; receiver queue length is not a substitute for the prescribed count.

obligations.statement: Compute chunk completion as timestamp plus decoded duration minus the latest output delay.
obligations.condition: Recomputing server-side completion times
obligations.notes: Uses the latest reported delay, not a frozen value from the original send.

obligations.statement: Derive chunk duration from decoded samples per channel and that chunk's original sample rate.
obligations.condition: Calculating outstanding completion times across formats
obligations.notes: A per-chunk duration ledger requirement; in-place format updates do not retrospectively reinterpret old chunks.

obligations.statement: Start the count empty and reset it on player clear or end.
obligations.condition: Initializing or resetting the player buffer ledger
obligations.notes: One ledger-reset rule with explicit triggers; it does not require clearing the client queue on every stream/start.

obligations.statement: Recalculate completion times for all chunks since the last reset on a delay update, including previously excluded chunks.
obligations.condition: Receiving changed output_delay_ms
obligations.notes: Previously completed/excluded chunks may re-enter the outstanding count after a delay decrease. An append-only currently-queued list would not be sufficient.

obligations.statement: Preserve count and prior chunk durations across an in-place stream/start.
obligations.condition: Updating an already active stream configuration
obligations.notes: Configuration updates are not ledger resets. This is independent of the receiving SDK's retained decoded-chunk test.

obligations.statement: Convert perceived volume to sample gain with amplitude=(volume/100)^1.5.
obligations.condition: Applying player volume to decoded samples
obligations.notes: The numeric curve is independently checked at multiple settings. It does not prove subjective loudness or correction inaudibility on hardware.

obligations.statement: Apply volume changes over a short ramp rather than an instantaneous gain step.
obligations.condition: Changing effective player gain
obligations.notes: The test verifies the implemented 5-ms gain sequence, mute transitions and input ownership; 5 ms is an implementation choice, not a new protocol constant.

obligations.statement: Do not clear mute when changing volume.
obligations.condition: Remote, group or local volume changes
obligations.notes: Native group-volume and exact player-command state checks retain mute while volume changes, including volume zero.

obligations.statement: Include the player support object when offering player@v1.
obligations.condition: Advertising the player role in client/hello
obligations.notes: The typed role support wrapper is exercised against strict independent peers. Generic support-key naming for other roles remains in the core inventory.

obligations.statement: Advertise a nonempty supported_formats array.
obligations.condition: Offering player capability
obligations.notes: Config rejects an explicit empty list and native PCM/FLAC/Opus negotiation exercises nonempty offers. No claim covers arbitrary custom decoder correctness.

obligations.statement: Preserve supported_formats preference order, with the first entry preferred.
obligations.condition: Serializing application-provided player formats
obligations.notes: The exact observed encrypted hello for every player-containing supported-role subset under both suites retains two independently specified formats in their supplied preference order, rather than inferring preference from the server-selected codec.

obligations.statement: Use the defined codec/string and channel/rate/bit-depth integer schema in player format objects.
obligations.condition: Advertising formats, reporting a preference or receiving stream/start
obligations.notes: One shared format-object grammar, not three independent pass counts. Only validated SDK-supported combinations are advertised; this does not require every possible sample rate or channel count.

obligations.statement: Ignore Opus bit depth when matching advertised, preferred and selected formats.
obligations.condition: The codec identifier is opus
obligations.notes: Unit matching changes only Opus bit depth across signed integer extremes; receive-side stream/start reaches a custom factory for those equivalents. Codec/rate/channel mismatches and PCM depth changes remain rejected. The separately typed field grammar is not waived.

obligations.statement: Advertise integer buffer_capacity in outstanding encoded chunk/header bytes.
obligations.condition: Reporting player support
obligations.notes: The emitted integer advertises the configured encoded-byte bound. Server outstanding accounting remains in P20; decoded-float memory and device queue lengths are not this field's units.

obligations.statement: List at least PCM or FLAC even when also offering Opus.
obligations.condition: Advertising supported player codecs
obligations.notes: Config enforces the baseline and the native Opus offer includes PCM. Optional Opus is additional, not a substitute for baseline interoperability.

obligations.statement: Optionally offer both PCM and FLAC.
obligations.condition: Selecting a player capability profile
obligations.notes: Defaults select this permitted combination. The permission is not a requirement that every configured player list both codecs.

obligations.statement: Optionally offer Opus alongside a baseline codec.
obligations.condition: Opus is included in configured supported_formats
obligations.notes: The SDK implements but does not request Opus by default. Patent/deployment context is a separate reviewed source note, not a wire negotiation requirement.

obligations.statement: Support FLAC on the Sendspin server.
obligations.condition: Serving compliant player capabilities
obligations.notes: A distinct server codec duty; successful client decoding does not implement a server encoder.

obligations.statement: Support PCM on the Sendspin server.
obligations.condition: Serving compliant player capabilities
obligations.notes: Separate from the client's requirement to advertise at least one baseline codec.

obligations.statement: Optionally support Opus on the Sendspin server.
obligations.condition: Choosing server encoder support
obligations.notes: The player is not told server codec capabilities; this permission does not authorize inventing a new server capability exchange.

obligations.statement: Decode PCM samples as little-endian signed two's-complement integers.
obligations.condition: The built-in PCM decoder is used
obligations.notes: Signed extrema and zero vectors verify decoding. A replacement decoder remains responsible for the codec contents it claims to support.

obligations.statement: Interpret PCM24 as packed three-byte samples.
obligations.condition: Receiving negotiated 24-bit PCM with a built-in decoder
obligations.notes: Three-byte sign extension is tested separately from ordinary 16-bit decoding.

obligations.statement: Preserve interleaved channel/frame order while decoding PCM.
obligations.condition: Receiving multichannel PCM
obligations.notes: Fixed independently authored interleaved samples distinguish every channel and frame for PCM16/packed PCM24 at 2, 3 and 8 channels, including negative samples. No mono vector or range-only fuzz result is substituted for channel identity.

obligations.statement: Reject partial PCM frames rather than splice codec units across audio chunks.
obligations.condition: Validating a built-in PCM chunk
obligations.notes: Chunk length is checked against sample width times channels. This is a per-chunk grammar rule, not the server's outstanding-byte ledger.

obligations.statement: Decode only complete FLAC frames within each chunk.
obligations.condition: Using the built-in FLAC decoder
obligations.notes: The exact frame vector and truncated-frame rejection are targeted evidence; exhaustive malformed FLAC parity/fuzzing remains outside this pass.

obligations.statement: Require a FLAC codec_header carrying fLaC followed by STREAMINFO.
obligations.condition: Starting FLAC; content validation uses the built-in factory
obligations.notes: Presence is enforced before every factory; built-ins validate STREAMINFO and negotiated values. A custom factory owns codec-specific contents, not the shared Base64 wire syntax.

obligations.statement: Treat each Opus chunk as exactly one bare packet, without a container.
obligations.condition: Receiving Opus audio
obligations.notes: Bare RFC packet vectors cover one frame and CBR/VBR/count-coded multiframe packets through 120 ms, exact decoded counts, empty/structurally truncated/over-duration packets and identifiable container headers. Multiple frames in one packet are valid. Arbitrary concatenated bytes can themselves be a valid packet; no impossible packet-provenance oracle or exhaustive codec-parity claim is made.

obligations.statement: Forbid codec_header presence for PCM and Opus.
obligations.condition: Receiving stream/start for PCM or Opus
obligations.notes: Even an empty present field is rejected before a replacement decoder. Absence differs from empty contents or null.

obligations.statement: Use standard RFC 4648 Base64 codec_header syntax with required padding and no ignored non-alphabet characters.
obligations.condition: Receiving or decoding a codec_header string
obligations.notes: This review reproduced ignored CR/LF and unchecked custom-factory syntax, then fixed both. Round-trip canonical standard Base64 is checked before factory dispatch and independently by the public built-in decoder; no operator-token leniency applies.

obligations.statement: Send whole codec units without spanning one unit across audio chunks.
obligations.condition: Encoding player binary payloads
obligations.notes: The server encoder must construct the specified wire units; defensive client decode checks do not implement or certify every sender encoder.

obligations.statement: Emit the player state object only while the player role is active.
obligations.condition: Sending client/state
obligations.notes: Exact encrypted full-state observations for all 64 active-role subsets and repeated removal/reactivation explicitly exclude player while inactive; retained player preferences do not leak its object.

obligations.statement: Send a full player state update whenever a player-state field changes.
obligations.condition: Local controls or server commands change player state
obligations.notes: The native trace compares exact full echoes and one Save per change, including while unavailable. The local delay setter/restart path is separately exercised; arbitrary application callback quality is not certified.

obligations.statement: Include integer volume in 0..100 when volume is offered.
obligations.condition: Player state advertises the volume command
obligations.notes: The current SDK always offers volume and verifies full echoes including zero and 100; no configurable read-only amplifier profile is implied.

obligations.statement: Include boolean muted when mute is offered.
obligations.condition: Player state advertises the mute command
obligations.notes: Exact typed true/false echoes are checked independently of volume changes.

obligations.statement: Always include the current integer output_delay_ms in player state, independent of command settability.
obligations.condition: Reporting an active player's state
obligations.notes: One required-output-field contract shared across the schema and capability explanation. Clamp/persistence are distinct P06 obligations. The present profile offers all three commands, not an untested read-only variant.

obligations.statement: Report required_lead_time_ms as a nonnegative integer startup-trigger-to-full-first-chunk hint.
obligations.condition: Reporting player timing state
obligations.notes: The fixed 35-ms field and its independence from output delay are observed. Actual reliable warmup calibration remains P08 measurement work, not a schema pass.

obligations.statement: Report min_buffer_ms as a nonnegative integer requested ongoing buffer hint.
obligations.condition: Reporting player timing state
obligations.notes: The emitted 20-ms value is checked, not claimed empirically sufficient for every network/backend. Distribution-based derivation remains separately reviewed in P08.

obligations.statement: Advertise supported_commands as a subset of volume, mute and set_output_delay.
obligations.condition: Sending player state capabilities
obligations.notes: The SDK's selected subset is the full three-command set. The empty-set permission does not require adding mutable command-subset configuration.

obligations.statement: Use only an advertised supported format when overriding the current format preference.
obligations.condition: A player reports the optional format preference
obligations.notes: Preference changes use Format.Matches against Config.Formats and are observed on the wire. Object grammar and Opus bit-depth matching have their own shared obligations.

obligations.statement: Interpret absent format preference as no local override.
obligations.condition: Player state omits format
obligations.notes: This optional-field meaning does not require an invented server capability negotiation or a new public preference-reset API.

obligations.statement: Persist nondefault player volume across reboots.
obligations.condition: Recreating a player from local persistent settings
obligations.notes: Public SetVolume changes to 17, then the first connection is stopped and a new Client with a newly opened FileStore is constructed. The nondefault value is checked before connection, on the real reference receive path after reconnect, and on disk with preserved identity/trust.

obligations.statement: Persist mute across reboots.
obligations.condition: Recreating a player after a saved mute change
obligations.notes: Public SetMuted(true), nondefault delay and volume survive actual FileStore/New-client restart and reference-observed reconnect; this is no longer a default-valued identity roundtrip or memory-only Save assertion.

obligations.statement: Do not assume volume or mute is unchanged after reconnection.
obligations.condition: A player reconnects
obligations.notes: Server fresh-state handling is not established by the client's local settings store.

obligations.statement: Send only player commands listed in the latest received supported_commands.
obligations.condition: Selecting a player command
obligations.notes: The sender consults its latest state snapshot; the client's ignore behavior is a separate receiving obligation.

obligations.statement: Ignore commands absent from the client's current offered set.
obligations.condition: An active player receives an unoffered command
obligations.notes: Unknown/unoffered command bodies cannot become actionable or cause persistence/echo. Known offered commands retain exact argument validation; arbitrary dynamic capability subsets are not implemented.

obligations.statement: Require a string command discriminator before applying the unoffered-command ignore rule.
obligations.condition: Receiving a player command object
obligations.notes: Missing/null/wrongly typed command selectors are malformed, not future command extensions.

obligations.statement: For volume commands require only the integer volume argument in 0..100.
obligations.condition: The offered command is volume
obligations.notes: Required/forbidden known argument combinations form one discriminator-specific schema; unknown informational fields stay ignorable.

obligations.statement: For mute commands require only the boolean mute argument, preserving false.
obligations.condition: The offered command is mute
obligations.notes: Zero/false presence is not inferred from truthiness; irrelevant known arguments remain prohibited.

obligations.statement: For set_output_delay require only the integer output_delay_ms argument.
obligations.condition: The offered command is set_output_delay
obligations.notes: Type/presence is distinct from the mandatory clamping policy in shared P06.02. Typed extreme integers are clamped, not rejected as another argument shape.

obligations.statement: Do not send player commands before the initial client/state.
obligations.condition: The player connection has not yet reported operational state
obligations.notes: This ordering duty is on the remote sender, not an invented client capability ACK.

obligations.statement: Choose a stream format from the client's advertised supported_formats.
obligations.condition: Sending player stream/start
obligations.notes: The server's selection duty does not replace the client's checking of the received proposal. Preference policy is separately classified in P22.

obligations.statement: Reject a selected player format that does not match an advertised format.
obligations.condition: Validating a player stream/start proposal
obligations.notes: Receive tests vary one nonadvertised codec/rate/channel/PCM-depth dimension at a time, check ErrProtocol before factory use or stream activation, and provide valid canonical FLAC header presence so another check cannot mask codec-matching failure.

obligations.statement: Prefer the player's current requested format when it can be produced for the track.
obligations.condition: Choosing a format for stream/start with a player override
obligations.notes: The preference is conditional on server producibility, not a client guarantee that every advertised codec will be served.

obligations.statement: Otherwise prefer the highest-priority advertised format that can be produced.
obligations.condition: No producible player override is selected
obligations.notes: A server selection recommendation, distinct from preserving the client's offered list order.

obligations.statement: Optionally select a different advertised entry when track/operator conditions warrant it.
obligations.condition: An alternate format avoids resampling or satisfies a warranted policy
obligations.notes: The exception does not permit an unadvertised format or erase the recommended default policy.

obligations.statement: Optionally change formats for a later track using a new stream/start.
obligations.condition: A later track warrants another advertised format
obligations.notes: Client buffer preservation and per-received-chunk format handling remain separate P11 obligations.

obligations.statement: Re-derive active stream format when player preference changes and send stream/start if the format changed.
obligations.condition: Preference changes during an active player stream
obligations.notes: One conditional reconfiguration transaction; no change need be sent when the newly derived format is identical.

obligations.statement: Apply an idle player's changed preference to the next stream start.
obligations.condition: A preference changes with no active stream
obligations.notes: No immediate client stream or synthetic restart is required while idle.

obligations.statement: Interpret heterogeneous-client encoding as a server capability consequence, not a client resampler obligation.
obligations.condition: Serving grouped players with different formats
obligations.notes: The explanatory separate-encoding sentence does not mandate one physical encoder instance per client or add source capture to this SDK.

obligations.statement: Do not infer remotely settable volume merely from a reported volume value.
obligations.condition: The latest supported_commands omits volume
obligations.notes: Settability and reportability are separate. This is not a missing SDK command-capability setter.

obligations.statement: Do not infer remotely settable mute merely from reported muted state.
obligations.condition: The latest supported_commands omits mute
obligations.notes: Independent mute capability inference must use the advertised command set.

obligations.statement: Optionally display reported values as read-only without offering remote controls.
obligations.condition: A player reports a non-settable value
obligations.notes: A server/operator UI permission; receiving SDK artwork/metadata does not implement that UI.

obligations.statement: Optionally report volume without offering the matching command.
obligations.condition: Choosing a read-only volume capability profile
obligations.notes: The current profile offers all player commands. This optional alternate amplifier profile is deliberately not exposed as configurable capability state.

obligations.statement: Optionally report muted state without offering the matching command.
obligations.condition: Choosing a read-only mute capability profile
obligations.notes: The permission does not require the SDK to implement arbitrary runtime command-subset changes.

obligations.statement: Hold at most one admitted connection under the selected single-holder policy.
obligations.condition: Parallel pairing admission is not selected
obligations.notes: Admission waits for the previous worker/session to finish before handing over. Fake-output ownership is not a strict physical tail/flush measurement for approximate Oto.

obligations.statement: Classify the current declared activity set by its highest rank: playback, then pairing, then idle.
obligations.condition: Publishing or updating an admitted holder's priority
obligations.notes: Rank publication and later rank changes are checked independently from deciding a new arbitration. One shared current-rank invariant avoids double counting the same activity-update rule.

obligations.statement: Persist the server_id of the most recent admitted holder declaring playback.
obligations.condition: An accepted holder initially declares or later enters playback
obligations.notes: Selection, preservation on demotion and FileStore/New-client reload are checked. Inadmissible candidates do not acquire this history by merely announcing playback.

obligations.statement: Keep a new connection provisional until its first admissible activation after the handshake.
obligations.condition: A new server connection is being authenticated/activated
obligations.notes: Actual incomplete handshakes reserve protected provisional state, and malformed/unauthorized activations cannot acquire the holder. This is not a socket-flood resilience guarantee.

obligations.statement: Do not apply priority arbitration to an inadmissible activation.
obligations.condition: Activation shape, roles or credential permissions fail
obligations.notes: A locked admission mutex is a deterministic barrier: invalid peers are refused without entering it, changing trust/history or retiring the current holder.

obligations.statement: Accept an admissible higher-ranked incoming connection unless an explicit exception applies.
obligations.condition: Incoming priority exceeds the current holder and no attempt-protection exception applies
obligations.notes: Playback replaces an idle holder. Attempt protection and the chosen single-holder pairing policy remain separate, explicit exceptions.

obligations.statement: Accept an admissible equal-ranked incoming connection outside the special idle/protection rules.
obligations.condition: Incoming and current non-idle priority are equal with no protected attempt
obligations.notes: The equal-playback case replaces the holder; it is not generalized to an unconditional idle reconnect takeover.

obligations.statement: Reject an incoming connection ranked below the admitted holder.
obligations.condition: Both activations are admissible and the incoming rank is lower
obligations.notes: The native idle-against-playback case observes concurrent_attempt and unchanged holder/trust. Exact refusal messages are separately classified in CN16.

obligations.statement: Do not displace a started pairing attempt with incoming playback.
obligations.condition: client/pair-init has started the current attempt
obligations.notes: Tests exercise protection before the actual first write returns and the opposite already-decided handoff ordering. A declared pairing activity alone is not the attempt-start definition.

obligations.statement: Do not displace a started pairing attempt with an incoming pairing connection.
obligations.condition: A second server tries pairing during the protected attempt
obligations.notes: A second independent native pairing candidate receives concurrent_attempt, actually disconnects/releases its SDK slot, reveals no finalize/record and leaves the original started attempt protected and usable. The original attempt subsequently completes normally.

obligations.statement: When both holders are idle, admit only an incoming last-playback identity over a different existing identity.
obligations.condition: Both declared activity sets are empty
obligations.notes: The previously missing duplicate socket with the already-last-playback holder identity is explicitly rejected through the public inbound handler, closed and released without retiring/displacing the holder. Existing native tests separately cover idle keep and incoming-last-playback takeover. The duplicate peer shares the Noise primitive, not SDK framing.

obligations.statement: Do not rerun admission arbitration on later activity updates of the admitted holder.
obligations.condition: A subsequent activation changes activities, including escalation
obligations.notes: The test holds admission locked while the same holder enters/leaves/re-enters playback. Rank/history still update for future comparisons through shared CN06.02.

obligations.statement: Drop a provisional connection that has not delivered its first activation within the capped 30-second budget.
obligations.condition: Waiting for first server/activate after WebSocket establishment
obligations.notes: Noise consumes the same initial budget; actor startup cannot restart it. Shorter local timeouts are allowed. This is not a bound on arbitrary pre-upgrade HTTP clients or blocking application/native calls.

obligations.statement: Notify a displaced non-pairing holder with client/goodbye another_server.
obligations.condition: A new admissible connection replaces the normal holder
obligations.notes: Rekey quiet-period gates defer application goodbye until activation rather than send it with forbidden timing or stale keys.

obligations.statement: Notify a displaced pairing handshake with pair/abort concurrent_attempt instead of ordinary goodbye.
obligations.condition: Displacement wins before a pairing attempt becomes protected
obligations.notes: A native holder is gated after hello and while publishing its admitted activation, before pair-init protection starts. Incoming playback decides retirement; release produces exactly pair/abort concurrent_attempt, no pair-init/finalize, and the replacement remains usable.

obligations.statement: Notify a rejected non-pairing incoming connection with client/goodbye concurrent_attempt.
obligations.condition: Normal priority arbitration rejects an admissible incoming peer
obligations.notes: This authenticated reason path is not proof for the separately unresolved pre-Noise resource-cap closure policy.

obligations.statement: Close the displaced or rejected non-pairing connection after its goodbye.
obligations.condition: Normal-holder displacement or normal incoming priority refusal has been notified
obligations.notes: The reference disconnection events and released previous output are explicit; physical hardware output-tail guarantees are not inferred.

obligations.statement: Close a displaced pairing handshake after its concurrent_attempt abort.
obligations.condition: An unprotected old pairing handshake has been displaced
obligations.notes: The same deterministic native pre-attempt retirement boundary observes actual old-peer disconnection and one remaining SDK session after abort, rather than merely a returned unit error. Started attempts remain protected, as separately tested.

obligations.statement: Support storage of at least five pairing records.
obligations.condition: Choosing and using record capacity
obligations.notes: The test initializes and preserves five records at configured capacity five, then makes one valid replacement. Resource caps and eviction predicates are linked shared CN15 atoms.

obligations.statement: Optionally support more than five pairing records.
obligations.condition: Selecting a larger local record capacity
obligations.notes: The SDK defaults to 16 and allows a bounded larger capacity. These local limits are not protocol-wide maximums, and the permission adds no minimum above five.

obligations.statement: Treat selection of an unused eviction victim as implementation-defined.
obligations.condition: More than one stored record is evictable
obligations.notes: Oldest unprotected record is the chosen policy. The illustrative least-recently-used example does not mandate an LRU database or permit eviction of open records.

obligations.statement: Do not invent a required wire notification for eviction of an unused record.
obligations.condition: Removing an unprotected stored record at capacity
obligations.notes: Eviction needs no signal. The next initial credential lookup follows the separately specified Sentinel fallback contract (CN23), not a synthetic unpair message to a nonexistent open peer.

obligations.statement: Implement all three pairing methods on the Sendspin server.
obligations.condition: Implementing a Sendspin server
obligations.notes: WebSocket acceptance does not turn the SDK into a Sendspin server or require server-side CPace/operator UI.

obligations.statement: Implement and offer the mandatory Pairing PSK method.
obligations.condition: Advertising client pairing support
obligations.notes: Native pairing succeeds and the peer observes the exact PSK-only method descriptor even without a player role.

obligations.statement: Optionally implement additional static or dynamic code-based pairing methods.
obligations.condition: Selecting the device's pairing method profile
obligations.notes: This SDK profile deliberately implements neither code method. Conditional code-flow duties below cite this actual unselected permission; the separate out-channel recommendations are not silently waived.

obligations.statement: Use a Sentinel-keyed connection for code-based pairing.
obligations.condition: A code-based method is implemented and selected
obligations.notes: A conditional flow requirement, not a claim that an unoffered PAKE is implemented or that Sentinel by itself authenticates an operator-known peer.

obligations.statement: Do not reveal the new code-pairing PSK before server_kc verifies.
obligations.condition: Completing an implemented code-based PAKE method
obligations.notes: This PAKE confirmation boundary is not interchangeable with PSK-method direct finalize or ordinary Noise message 2.

obligations.statement: Reveal a code-pairing long-term PSK only as wrapped_psk sealed under the CPace output.
obligations.condition: A selected code method has verified server_kc
obligations.notes: No wrapper implementation is claimed. The PSK method's directly carried secret has a different, separately authenticated flow.

obligations.statement: Treat the static-versus-dynamic out-channel distinction as method context.
obligations.condition: Interpreting the advertised pairing profile
obligations.notes: Pairing PSK uses no code presentation channel. Shared-output suspension for an actual dynamic code is separately classified in R07; this overview is not a physical output guarantee.

obligations.statement: Prefer dynamic rather than static code pairing on a device with a usable out-channel.
obligations.condition: An embedding device has a usable display or speaker out-channel
obligations.notes: R:5 makes extra code methods optional, but R:19 separately makes the dynamic-over-static preference an uppercase SHOULD for usable out-channels. The historical PSK-only assessment remains unchanged. The user-requested optional PIN extension now recommends the dynamic display profile and supports static devices separately; physical operator-interface and independent security acceptance remain open, and no frozen assessment is promoted by its tests. See docs/pin-pairing.md and rc1-review-decisions.md.

obligations.statement: Consider qr_code emission on a QR-capable display when choosing a dynamic-code product profile.
obligations.condition: The embedding device has a QR-capable pairing display
obligations.notes: The second R:19 sentence says lowercase 'should also offer', unlike the preceding uppercase SHOULD. The pinned template.md Normative Language section applies BCP 14 only to uppercase keywords; this sentence is descriptive product guidance, not an independently elevated BCP-14 SHOULD. Dynamic code remains unoffered. This disposition does not weaken R01.08's uppercase recommendation, the defined qr_code grammar for implementations that offer it, or R15.04's separate uppercase MUST for a physically printed pairing PSK. See rc1-review-decisions.md for pinned context.

obligations.statement: Draw each device's pairing PSK from a CSPRNG.
obligations.condition: Provisioning new device credentials
obligations.notes: A focused AST policy guard verifies NewCredentials draws the pairing PSK via crypto/rand, and 64 generated device credentials guard empty/shared/reused values. This is generation-path/default regression evidence, not statistical entropy estimation or independent OS-CSPRNG certification.

obligations.statement: Do not use a shared fixed pairing-PSK default across devices.
obligations.condition: Manufacturing or generating device credentials
obligations.notes: Distinct-device generation independently checks pairing PSKs, private keys and identities are not shared/reused/default Sentinel/zero values; ordinary interop alone would not expose a shared device default.

obligations.statement: Persist the device pairing PSK across reboots.
obligations.condition: Reloading the same device's local credentials
obligations.notes: FileStore reload and Client recreation retain this secret. MemoryStore alone does not meet device restart persistence.

obligations.statement: Do not consume or rotate the device pairing PSK merely because pairing succeeds.
obligations.condition: Persisting a successful long-term server pairing
obligations.notes: Native re-pairing replaces only the long-term record and explicitly preserves pairing PSK/private identity. This does not require unbounded simultaneous record storage.

obligations.statement: Expose the operator's pairing PSK as a version-0 token with the client key, not as a bare PSK.
obligations.condition: Providing an out-of-band operator pairing credential
obligations.notes: PairingToken is the operator interface and ordinary formatting is redacted. Explicit secret serialization for a private Store is not operator presentation and is not prohibited by this clause.

obligations.statement: Keep the standing pairing PSK among handshake candidates even outside pairing activity.
obligations.condition: Resolving initial or rekey PSK selection
obligations.notes: A long-term-keyed live connection re-pairs through the standing pairing key without another hello or activity-gated candidate registration.

obligations.statement: Verify that the matched key is the pairing PSK before starting pairing_psk; refuse a method mismatch with method_not_supported.
obligations.condition: An otherwise admissible activation reaches the pairing-method/key compatibility check
obligations.notes: The native Sentinel-keyed injected pairing_psk activation emits method_not_supported without pair-init/finalize or persisted trust. The strict native peer may then close because its own state machine did not request pairing; the scripted actual rekey/category trace separately proves the SDK leaves a well-typed unsupported-method channel usable and respects earlier refusal precedence.

obligations.statement: Carry the PSK-method long_term_psk as exactly 32 bytes in unpadded 43-character Base64URL, without wrapped_psk.

obligations.statement: Discard audio scheduled during a shared-output code attempt without ending the stream.

obligations.statement: Use approximately two minutes as the recommended default attempt timeout.

obligations.statement: Optionally cancel pairing at any point with a replacing server/activate.

obligations.statement: After local abort silently discard in-flight pairing messages only until the next activation.

obligations.statement: Do not count an abandoned code attempt as a failed pairing-window attempt.

obligations.notes: No code window is implemented. The counter exception is retained as a conditional duty, not confused with PSK retry/index counting.

obligations.statement: Count an abandoned code attempt toward round limiting only if code emission already occurred.
obligations.condition: An implemented code-method attempt ends by cancellation
obligations.notes: A code-emission counter condition, unrelated to the count of received pairing activations carried by PSK pair-init.

obligations.statement: Send user_cancelled abort before a cancelling activation when the operator cancels.

obligations.statement: Apply a server timeout while waiting for client/pair-init.
obligations.condition: The selected attempt has not yet started

obligations.statement: Reset the pairing activation count after a new Noise handshake.

obligations.statement: Silently discard client pairing indices lower than the server's activation count.

obligations.statement: Close silently on locally detected code-method share/commitment/binding/wrapper protocol errors.
obligations.condition: An additional code pairing method is implemented and detects a protocol error

obligations.statement: Persist no code-method credentials after such a locally detected protocol error.
obligations.condition: An implemented code-flow protocol check fails
obligations.notes: The unselected MAY is cited directly; a successful PSK flow is not evidence of this conditional PAKE failure handling.

obligations.statement: Keep the connection open after a non-concurrent pairing abort.

obligations.notes: A same-direction barrier and successful subsequent native attempt establish liveness after ordinary aborts. This does not promise liveness when a separate network/protocol failure occurs.

obligations.statement: Give a late pair/abort no effect after the receiver has itself ended the attempt.

obligations.statement: Use concurrent_attempt to refuse another pairing connection during a protected attempt.

obligations.statement: Close the conflicting incoming pairing connection after concurrent_attempt.
obligations.condition: A protected-attempt collision has been refused
obligations.notes: The conflicting native pairing peer is observed disconnected and its SDK slot released before a holder usability barrier; no forced test-side disconnect substitutes for client closure.

obligations.statement: During a live attempt accept only defined server-permitted abort reasons, rejecting client-only/unknown or malformed values.
obligations.condition: Processing a server abort before the attempt has ended

obligations.statement: Abandon pending pairing on a valid remote abort without echoing or persisting it.
obligations.condition: A server-permitted reason aborts a live attempt
obligations.notes: Unit state/store assertions cover no local credential creation or invented echo; actor/network/liveness breadth is bounded by the linked cases.

obligations.statement: Treat a late client abort as ineffective after the server has itself ended the attempt.

obligations.statement: End the pairing transition with activation declaring the resulting activities and active roles.

obligations.statement: Persist the new long-term PSK bound to the authenticated client_id on the server.

obligations.statement: Refuse an otherwise admissible unoffered pairing method or emission format with method_not_supported.

obligations.statement: Optionally admit unpaired role/playback access under local policy.

obligations.statement: Treat the unpaired-access default as manufacturer/application policy, not a universal protocol default.

obligations.statement: Do not let remote messages change the locally owned unpaired-access setting.
obligations.condition: Receiving policy-shaped unknown fields or remote commands
obligations.notes: After inverse-valued fields in server/state and server/command and a same-direction barrier, disabled policy still denies playback and enabled policy still admits native-approved roles, without local Store changes. This adds no runtime toggle API.

obligations.condition: A device locally stops admitting access on which a live connection relies
obligations.notes: The obligation is a conditional mandatory client contract: an actual local withdrawal must close relying sessions with pairing_required. It does not require a particular setter API. This SDK's policy is immutable per Client and cannot withdraw access in place; remote fields cannot change it. Classification is complete, but an embedding product offering live withdrawal still needs a reviewed implementation and exact goodbye/closure evidence. Cancellation sends shutdown and is not a compliant substitute for that operation. Neither restart construction nor immutable-policy tests discharge this duty. Keep the mandatory review blocker; no runtime toggle or protocol behavior is added. See rc1-review-decisions.md.

obligations.statement: Optionally restart an existing unpaired connection to advertise newly enabled access.
obligations.condition: A runtime local enable-policy operation is selected
obligations.notes: No live enable operation or restart-on-enable policy is implemented. This permission does not justify weakening the separate withdrawal clause.

obligations.condition: The operator has approved a client_id

obligations.statement: Allow the operator to revoke unpaired-client approval.
obligations.condition: Operator approval is implemented
obligations.notes: A remote administration capability, not a new local SDK control command.

obligations.condition: An approved client becomes paired
obligations.notes: The resulting trust is the new pairing, not an approval flag in the client's local credential snapshot.

obligations.statement: Optionally hold an unapproved connection idle until approval or pairing.
obligations.condition: An unpaired client has no operator approval
obligations.notes: Empty activities are a valid idle state; this is not blanket authorization to activate roles.

obligations.statement: Identify and present unapproved clients to the operator.
obligations.condition: A server knows an unapproved client

obligations.statement: Clearly distinguish unpaired/unapproved clients from paired or approved ones in the server UI.
obligations.condition: Presenting clients to an operator
obligations.notes: A familiar claimed name is not authentication. This UI distinction is separate from cryptographic key binding.

obligations.notes: The SDK advertises methods but does not implement remote operator action controls.

obligations.statement: Treat Sentinel encryption as confidentiality/replay protection, not operator-known peer authentication.

obligations.statement: Reverse 9-to-2 transliteration, re-pad to a multiple of eight and Base32-decode operator input.
obligations.condition: Decoding a version-0 token body
obligations.notes: The matrix covers absent, partial and full operator padding, optional/mixed-case prefix and both ordinary/transliterated alphabets. No stricter wire decoder is substituted for this operator interface.

obligations.statement: Reject malformed or short version-0 payloads without returning partial credentials.

obligations.notes: One shared version-1 representation requirement, not evidence of code derivation or rendering. The current version-0 parser deliberately does not claim this interface.

obligations.statement: Keep supplied RGB palette values without treating primary/accent as client-generated contrast-adjusted colors.

obligations.statement: Distinguish a timestamp-only applied empty palette from a removed role's absent state.
obligations.condition: The host reads current palette after clear or role removal
obligations.notes: Shared replacement/removal rules produce this library read-model distinction; it is not a new on-wire clear opcode.

obligations.statement: Optionally ease/blend into a pending palette around its timestamp.

obligations.statement: Ensure background_dark has at least 4.5:1 contrast with white text.

obligations.statement: Ensure at least 4.5:1 contrast between background_dark and on_dark when both are present.

obligations.statement: Ensure background_light has at least 4.5:1 contrast with black text.

obligations.statement: Ensure at least 4.5:1 contrast between background_light and on_light when both are present.

obligations.statement: Ensure on_dark has at least 4.5:1 contrast with black text for alternate-background use.

obligations.statement: Ensure on_light has at least 4.5:1 contrast with white text for alternate-background use.

obligations.statement: Declare one to four artwork channel objects in channel-index order.

obligations.statement: Use source album/artist/none and include format/width/height for an enabled channel.
obligations.condition: Constructing an enabled artwork declaration

obligations.statement: Optionally truncate the declaration after its last enabled channel.
obligations.condition: Unused trailing channel indices
obligations.notes: A one-channel emitted declaration omits the three trailing positions; an explicit trailing none entry may also be omitted by the matching server echo. Tests compare effective stream configuration without inventing four active channels.

obligations.statement: Close on a client artwork declaration longer than four channels.
obligations.condition: Receiving an oversized client channels array
obligations.notes: A server receive recommendation; the client rejects its own oversized configuration separately.

obligations.statement: Send no artwork data to a channel disabled by source none.
obligations.condition: The positional declaration disables the destination
obligations.notes: The receiver's channel guard is not certification of every server sender path.

obligations.statement: Support JPEG encoding.
obligations.condition: Producing artwork for an enabled client channel
obligations.notes: Server image-production obligation. Encoded-byte reception/hash tests do not certify arbitrary source-image processing.

obligations.statement: Support PNG encoding.
obligations.condition: Producing artwork for an enabled client channel
obligations.notes: Server image-production obligation. Encoded-byte reception/hash tests do not certify arbitrary source-image processing.

obligations.statement: Deliver images at exactly the declared channel width and height.
obligations.condition: Producing artwork for an enabled client channel
obligations.notes: Server image-production obligation. Encoded-byte reception/hash tests do not certify arbitrary source-image processing.

obligations.statement: Scale source images preserving aspect ratio to fit the declared rectangle.
